title: Rejected temporary-Datalog proposals paused for user confirmation instead of feeding back to the model for retry
description: Follow-up to 3cq, live repro 2026-07-08 session pid-0e8dc2f0: BYOK model omitted '.output answer'; validation rejected the proposal but the turn still paused with a confirmation card for a program that could never execute; approving replayed the rejection ('Temporary Datalog must output exactly answer(x:symbol).'). Fix: _propose_temporary_datalog returns status=rejected (code tool.proposal_rejected) with diagnostics + the authoring contract in the message; the harness's normal tool loop feeds it back so the model revises and re-proposes within the same turn (bounded by max_rounds=20). Only safe_to_confirm proposals pause for the user.
close_reason: Rejected proposals now bounce back to the model with diagnostics + authoring contract for same-turn retry; only executable proposals reach the confirmation card. Committed.

title: PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers need a trustworthy way to ask questions about a DEXPI 1.3 source file without receiving non-deterministic or hallucinated answers from graph RAG or free-form LLM QA.

The current repository can extract a pyDEXPI full graph, persist a canonical base fact layer, derive an initial generic graph utility layer, and run a narrow pump discharge-path verifier. What it does not yet prove is whether Souffle can serve as the deterministic QA and verification engine over those generated facts.

The user wants to preserve the key product principle: LLMs may help classify, route, and explain questions later, but compliance answers must come from deterministic query outputs. Before adding any LLM integration, the backend must demonstrate that generated Datalog facts can answer useful P&ID topology questions, expose missing facts and predicates clearly, and preserve query results as auditable artifacts.

## Solution

Build the first deterministic P&ID QA query layer around generated derived graph semantics.

The solution should enrich the derived Datalog fact surface with enough base object facts to make query output interpretable, starting with node and node_label facts. It should add a small query corpus that records supported, unsupported, and future candidate P&ID QA questions in an engine-portable way. It should add a CLI query harness that runs a supported known-object topology query against an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file using Souffle, prints readable terminal output, persists the combined Souffle program, persists a JSON result artifact, and keeps raw Souffle output files in an internal output directory.

The first supported query should compare reachable targets and downstream_reference targets for a known source object ID. The first near-term unsupported query should be a pump discharge path classification question. A harder manual-valve-before-check-valve question should be recorded as a future candidate so the system does not overfit only easy queries.

The query corpus should explicitly encode determinism requirements and LLM role constraints. LLM integration is out of scope for this PRD, but the corpus should make future LLM routing safe by documenting that LLMs may classify questions, route to deterministic queries, and explain deterministic results, but may not produce compliance answers without deterministic query output.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to ask deterministic questions about a DEXPI 1.3 source file, so that I can trust the answer is repeatable and auditable.
2. As a process engineer, I want QA answers to come from deterministic query execution rather than free-form LLM generation, so that compliance answers do not vary between runs.
3. As a process engineer, I want to provide a known object ID and see what objects are reachable from it, so that I can inspect the topology around a specific P&ID object.
4. As a process engineer, I want to compare reachable targets with downstream_reference targets, so that I can understand whether the generic graph utility layer is too broad or too narrow.
5. As a process engineer, I want query output to show full object IDs and object labels, so that results are exact and still readable.
6. As a process engineer, I want empty query results to be treated as successful answers, so that no-result cases can teach us about isolated objects or missing semantics.
7. As a process engineer, I want a warning when the provided source ID is absent from node facts, so that I can distinguish an empty answer from a likely wrong ID.
8. As a process engineer, I want the system to clearly say when a question is unsupported, so that I do not receive a misleading answer.
9. As a process engineer, I want unsupported questions to explain whether facts or predicates are missing, so that I know what capability must be built next.
10. As a process engineer, I want future thermodynamic or hydraulic questions to be identified as requiring external calculation when appropriate, so that Datalog is not overclaimed as a physics engine.
11. As a process engineer, I want the near-term north-star query to trace and classify a centrifugal pump discharge path, so that the QA layer grows toward realistic P&ID review tasks.
12. As a process engineer, I want harder valve-ordering questions to remain visible as future candidates, so that the roadmap reflects realistic engineering concerns.
13. As a maintainer, I want graph_facts.json to remain the canonical base fact layer, so that extraction output stays stable and auditable.
14. As a maintainer, I want Souffle to be evaluated as the deterministic QA and verification engine, so that rule answers can be fast and repeatable.
15. As a maintainer, I want Python to orchestrate extraction, Datalog generation, Souffle execution, and artifact persistence, so that Python is not the source of truth for compliance answers.
16. As a maintainer, I want derived_graph_semantics.dl to include node and node_label facts, so that Datalog queries can produce readable P&ID information without falling back to graph_facts.json for every label.
17. As a maintainer, I want the query harness to operate on an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file first, so that the first slice directly tests the artifact users want to query.
18. As a maintainer, I want the long-term design to allow querying from graph_facts.json directly, so that later workflows can generate and query Datalog in one command.
19. As a maintainer, I want missing Souffle installation to produce a clear diagnostic, so that setup problems are not confused with query failures.
20. As a maintainer, I want Souffle syntax or runtime failures to be treated as failed query execution, so that invalid query programs are surfaced clearly.
21. As a maintainer, I want unsupported corpus entries to return structured unsupported diagnostics, so that unsupported questions are first-class product outputs rather than errors.
22. As a maintainer, I want the query corpus to be separate from compliance rule YAML, so that QA questions do not get confused with promoted validation rules.
23. As a maintainer, I want one YAML file per query corpus entry, so that each query can have its own lifecycle, documentation, and promotion status.
24. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include determinism metadata, so that the engine and source-of-truth assumptions are explicit.
25. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include allowed and disallowed LLM roles, so that future LLM integration does not bypass deterministic execution.
26. As a maintainer, I want query corpus entries to include engine candidates such as Souffle and ErgoAI, so that the query library stays portable across deterministic engines.
27. As a maintainer, I want ErgoAI to remain a future engine candidate rather than an immediate dependency, so that the first slice tests the fact model before changing reasoning engines.
28. As a maintainer, I want the first query harness to read the query corpus entry minimally, so that the corpus becomes load-bearing without requiring a generic query interpreter too early.
29. As a maintainer, I want the first supported query implementation to be explicit and narrow, so that the team learns from real query output before inventing a broad abstraction.
30. As a maintainer, I want the combined Souffle program that actually ran to be persisted, so that users can inspect and rerun the exact query.
31. As a maintainer, I want the generated temporary query Datalog text included in the JSON result artifact, so that query behavior remains explainable.
32. As a maintainer, I want raw Souffle output files kept in an internal subdirectory, so that advanced users can inspect them while the top-level output remains readable.
33. As a maintainer, I want query output files to be overwritten during early experimentation, so that the learning loop stays low-friction.
34. As a maintainer, I want persisted JSON query artifacts, so that query behavior can become regression-tested and compared across fixtures.
35. As a maintainer, I want terminal output for the first query, so that hands-on learning stays tangible.
36. As a future LLM integrator, I want a query corpus with supported and unsupported entries, so that an LLM can later classify and route questions safely.
37. As a future LLM integrator, I want deterministic query outputs to be the only source of compliance answers, so that natural-language explanations remain grounded.
38. As a future rule author, I want the query corpus to reveal missing predicates, so that the P&ID query library grows from real questions instead of imagined ontology.
39. As a future rule author, I want the CodeQL-style library idea to grow from supported queries, so that raw graph facts become stable engineering predicates, reusable path predicates, and validation templates only when needed.
40. As a reviewer, I want the first query corpus to include a future candidate that is too hard today, so that the project does not optimize only for easy topology questions.
41. As a reviewer, I want the query corpus to classify unsupported questions by reason, so that missing data, missing predicates, external calculations, and ambiguity are not conflated.
42. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between unsupported_missing_facts and unsupported_missing_predicates, so that the roadmap can separate extraction work from query-library work.
43. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between unsupported_external_calculation and deterministic graph QA, so that thermodynamics and hydraulics are not accidentally oversold.
44. As a reviewer, I want a clear distinction between needs_human_clarification and deterministic query execution, so that ambiguous engineering questions are handled honestly.
45. As a reviewer, I want the first deterministic QA seam to be tested through the CLI and persisted artifacts, so that behavior is verified at the same level users experience it.

## Implementation Decisions

- The canonical base fact layer remains graph_facts.json.
- Souffle is the current deterministic engine for the first QA viability slice.
- Python remains the orchestration Adapter for generation, execution, diagnostics, terminal rendering, and artifact persistence.
- LLM integration is explicitly deferred until deterministic tools and query corpus semantics are established.
- The derived graph semantics output should be enriched with node and node_label facts.
- The first query harness operates on an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file.
- The first supported query compares reachable and downstream_reference results for a known source object ID.
- The command should accept a query ID and load the corresponding query corpus entry.
- The command should support the first query ID with explicit implementation rather than a generic YAML-driven query interpreter.
- Unsupported query corpus entries should produce structured unsupported artifacts, not unknown-query errors.
- Missing Souffle should produce a clear diagnostic and failed status.
- Empty result sets should produce successful query artifacts.
- Source ID absence should produce a warning when node facts make validation possible, not a failed status.
- Terminal output should include full target IDs and labels.
- JSON output should include status, diagnostics, query metadata, source ID, generated query Datalog, combined program path, raw output directory, and result sets.
- The combined Souffle program should be persisted as a first-class artifact.
- Raw Souffle output files should be placed under an internal output subdirectory.
- Query output files may be overwritten during the viability phase.
- Query corpus entries should live under queries/corpus as separate YAML files.
- The first corpus entry should be compare_known_object_reachability with supported_deterministic status.
- The near-term target corpus entry should be classify_pump_discharge_path with unsupported_missing_predicates status.
- The advanced future candidate should be manual_valve_before_check_valve_with_exceptions with future_candidate status.
- Query corpus entries should include determinism metadata, current engine, future engine candidates, and LLM role constraints.
- ErgoAI should be documented as a future engine candidate for richer explanations, exceptions, and semantic-rule authoring, not adopted in the first slice.
- The long-term concept is a P&ID query library inspired by CodeQL: raw graph facts to stable engineering predicates to reusable path predicates to validation templates.
- The corpus should be engine-portable and should not make Souffle the only possible long-term reasoning engine.
- The near-term north-star query is pump discharge path classification rather than the more advanced manual-valve-before-check-valve query.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests should verify behavior through public interfaces and persisted artifacts, not private helper structure.
- The highest test seam for the first slice is the CLI query command over a generated derived graph semantics file.
- Tests should run the query command against a representative fixture and assert terminal-visible behavior plus persisted JSON artifact shape.
- Tests should verify that derive-graph-semantics emits node and node_label facts as part of the generated Datalog artifact.
- Tests should verify that the first supported query returns successful output even when one or both result sets are empty.
- Tests should verify that absent source IDs produce warning diagnostics rather than failed execution.
- Tests should verify missing Souffle handling if feasible without depending on the developer machine PATH; if not feasible, isolate that behavior behind the command seam with controlled PATH configuration.
- Tests should verify unsupported corpus entries return structured unsupported diagnostics.
- Tests should verify the combined Souffle program is persisted and includes the generated query Datalog.
- Tests should verify raw Souffle output files are placed under an internal subdirectory.
- Tests should verify the checked-in query corpus entries include determinism and LLM-role metadata.
- Existing prior art includes CLI-style tests for export-facts, derive-graph-semantics, verify-suite, verify-raw-fixture, and compile-rule.
- Existing prior art also includes persisted artifact assertions for graph facts, derived graph semantics, verifier results, and behavioral harness summaries.
- The tests should extend those existing black-box seams rather than introducing internal mocks.
- The first implementation should use red-green vertical slices: one behavior test, minimal implementation, repeat.

## Out of Scope

- LLM integration.
- Natural-language question classification.
- RAG or MCP routing.
- OmniTQA implementation.
- ErgoAI integration.
- A generic query language interpreter over YAML corpus files.
- Full support for arbitrary user-generated P&ID questions.
- Full compliance rule authoring.
- Thermodynamic, hydraulic, sizing, or simulation calculations.
- DEXPI 2.0 ingestion.
- Replacing graph_facts.json as the canonical base fact layer.
- Making Python the source of truth for compliance answers.
- Immutable production run directories for query artifacts.
- A polished process engineer UI.
- Full path provenance or ordered path reconstruction beyond what the first query needs.
- Supporting the advanced manual-valve-before-check-valve query in the first slice.
- Promoting unsupported corpus entries to trusted validation rules.

## Further Notes

The key product principle is: the LLM can help ask, route, and explain the question, but deterministic tools must answer compliance questions.

The first implementation should be treated as a Souffle QA viability slice. It should be allowed to reveal that current predicates are too broad, too narrow, or missing. That learning is valuable and should drive the next predicates in the P&ID query library.

The strongest external architecture analogues are CodeQL for layered query libraries and query metadata, OPA for deterministic policy decisions and diagnostics, osquery for exposing messy domain state through stable queryable relations, and Semgrep or dbt-style registries for curated query/rule corpora with examples and tests.

The most important immediate learning is whether generated Datalog artifacts can support useful known-object topology QA before the project invests in YAML-to-rule compilation, LLM routing, or a larger semantic-rule engine.

title: Delete legacy query corpus, rule compiler, and XML-normalization paths
description:
## Problem

After reorganizing the package by pipeline seams, several compatibility paths still keep old architecture alive:

- queries/corpus/ YAML query entries and the query-derived-graph corpus loader.
- rules/ YAML inputs and compiled rule artifacts used by compile-rule tests.
- pydexpi_datalog/_legacy/ XML-direct normalization and cache paths used by dry-run/review-only compatibility behavior.
- Legacy JSON rule evaluation and patch proposal paths that depend on XML-direct normalized objects rather than graph-mirrored facts or LLM-native logic requests.

These paths assume humans hand-author structured YAML/query/rule files. In the LLM-native architecture, the user-facing authoring seam is a logic request: the LLM drafts Datalog plus an English restatement as an in-memory or persisted logic-request artifact, while deterministic execution remains the answer source.

## What to build

Delete the legacy query corpus, rule compiler artifacts, and XML-direct normalization paths. Keep or replace only the behavior that still belongs in the current architecture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Delete queries/corpus/ and remove code/tests/docs that require YAML query-corpus entries.
- [ ] Delete rules/ and remove the compile-rule command, compiler tests, and compiled-rule fixture expectations unless a current non-legacy workflow still needs them.
- [ ] Delete pydexpi_datalog/_legacy/ and tests/_legacy/.
- [ ] Remove dry-run and review-only dependencies on legacy XML normalization/cache artifacts, or replace them with graph-facts/derived-semantics based behavior.
- [ ] Remove or rewrite legacy JSON rule evaluation and patch proposal tests that assume XML-direct normalized objects.
- [ ] Update README and docs so they describe the LLM-native logic-request path and no longer present YAML query/rule authoring as a supported workflow.
- [ ] Public CLI help no longer advertises removed commands.
- [ ] Full test suite passes after obsolete tests are removed or replaced.

## Notes

This is intentionally behavior-breaking cleanup. Do not treat it as a compatibility-preserving refactor. If a command or test only exists to preserve the old hand-authored YAML/query/rule workflow, remove it rather than moving it.

Keep the stable deterministic substrate:

- DEXPI source file to pyDEXPI full graph.
- graph_facts.json base fact artifact.
- graph_facts.dl and derived_graph_semantics.dl.
- BYOK logic requests that can draft Datalog and restatements against the approved predicate contract.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.8

title: Resolve source-rooted queries by deterministic object selectors
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-153 PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer

## What to build

Make source-rooted deterministic QA queries usable without requiring users to know internal graph node IDs. The query command should accept deterministic object selectors and resolve them through Datalog facts/predicates from the combined derived graph semantics artifact.

Allowed source selectors:

- --source-id for exact/debug/test use
- --source-tag for human-facing equipment tags such as P-4713
- --source-proteus-id for source Proteus IDs such as CentrifugalPump-1

Do not add --source-label. Class labels are too loose and commonly non-unique.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] query-derived-graph accepts --source-tag and --source-proteus-id for source-rooted supported queries.
- [ ] --source-id remains supported for exact tests and debugging.
- [ ] Source selector resolution uses Datalog output from the combined artifact, not Python parsing of graph_facts.json.
- [ ] Source-rooted supported queries fail clearly if no source selector is provided.
- [ ] If multiple selectors are provided and resolve to the same node, the query succeeds and records the resolved source ID.
- [ ] If multiple selectors resolve to different nodes, the query fails with a structured diagnostic.
- [ ] If a selector matches no node, the query fails with a structured diagnostic.
- [ ] If a selector matches multiple nodes, the query fails with an ambiguity diagnostic.
- [ ] Query corpus entries for compare_known_object_reachability and compare_direct_process_connections mark source selection as source-rooted.

## Notes

This bead should not add source-label selection and should not default source-rooted queries to the first graph node.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic source selectors for source-rooted queries. Validation: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests (81 tests OK).

title: Add whole-P&ID query mode without first-node defaults
description:
## Parent

- pydexpi-datalog-1-153 PRD: Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer

## What to build

Add query corpus and harness support for whole-P&ID deterministic queries that evaluate across the complete P&ID instead of treating an arbitrary graph node as a root.

Do not default source-rooted queries to the first node in the graph. NetworkX insertion order and container-like nodes such as ConceptualModel are not meaningful engineering defaults.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Query corpus metadata can distinguish source-rooted queries from whole_pid queries.
- [ ] Whole-P&ID queries run without requiring --source-id, --source-tag, or --source-proteus-id.
- [ ] Source-rooted queries still require an explicit source selector.
- [ ] The query harness rejects accidental first-node default behavior.
- [ ] A first whole-P&ID query entry exists in the corpus, focused on a realistic P&ID-wide question rather than generic reachability.
- [ ] Whole-P&ID query artifacts record that the scope was the whole P&ID, not a selected source node.
- [ ] Tests prove a whole-P&ID query can run or return a structured unsupported/future-candidate artifact without a source selector.

## Notes

This is likely the precursor to all-pump discharge-path classification. Keep it separate from source selector work so source-rooted and whole-P&ID query semantics remain explicit.
close_reason: Implemented whole-P&ID query scope metadata and future-candidate query artifacts without source selector defaults. Validation: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests (84 tests OK).

title: Emit human-readable node alias facts in derived graph semantics
description:
Add a thin alias layer to derived graph semantics so deterministic QA can keep node_id as the canonical topology key while exposing human-readable selectors for tests and terminal output.

Context:
- Parent PRD: pydexpi-datalog-1-153 Build a deterministic P&ID QA query layer.
- Current derived semantics emits node/1 and node_label/2 from graph_facts.json.
- UUID node IDs are correct for graph joins but hard for humans to inspect against P&ID/SVG/XML views.

What to build:
- Keep node_id as the canonical graph identity.
- Emit node_tag(id, tag) facts from node attribute tagName when present.
- Emit node_proteus_id(id, proteus_id) facts from node attribute proteusId when present.
- Consider emitting node_display_name(id, display) with a narrow deterministic fallback order: tagName, then proteusId, then label.
- Do not replace node_id in existing predicates.
- Do not parse SVG labels or introduce a generic identity resolver in this slice.

Acceptance criteria:
- derive-graph-semantics emits node_tag/2 for tagged graph objects.
- derive-graph-semantics emits node_proteus_id/2 for objects with proteusId.
- If node_display_name/2 is included, its fallback order is documented and tested.
- Existing node/1, node_label/2, and edge-family predicates continue to be emitted unchanged.
- Tests verify behavior through the CLI-generated derived_graph_semantics.dl artifact using representative graph_facts.json.
- Representative generated artifact is updated if this repo keeps one checked in.
close_reason: Completed: derive-graph-semantics now emits node_tag/2 from tagName and node_proteus_id/2 from proteusId while keeping node_id as the canonical graph identity. Updated representative derived_graph_semantics.dl, CLI artifact tests, and the derived graph semantics contract. Validation passed: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_derive_graph_semantics.py (4 tests OK) and .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests (58 tests OK).

title: PRD: Multi-diagram project workspace — page-navigated shell, resizable/zoomable panels, rule-pack browsing
description:
## Problem Statement

The current frontend is functionally correct but reads as a single-purpose chat widget bolted onto a rigid P&ID viewer, not a product a process engineer would return to across a real review workload. The right-hand P&ID panel has no zoom or pan — the drawing-faithful/auto-layout schematic renderer (`schematic-scene-view.tsx`) is a static SVG with a fixed `viewBox`, so an engineer cannot inspect a dense area of their own drawing. Nothing is resizable: the left rail, chat column, and P&ID panel are fixed-width CSS regions. The left rail is a narrow icon-only strip by explicit prior design choice (a code comment states collapsing it further "isn't worth the added interaction cost"), and its icons don't communicate their purpose — a `SlidersHorizontal` glyph for Rule Packs reads as a filter control, and a `Clock` for session history looks like a time/scheduling feature. Rule packs live in a small overlay flyout with no standalone browsable surface. Most fundamentally, the product has no concept of a project: `review project` exists only as an aspirational glossary term ("a future signed-in workspace"), a chat is hard-bound to exactly one uploaded diagram, and there is no way to group review work across multiple P&IDs, PFDs, or other diagram types over time.

## Solution

Rebuild the app shell and its navigation model, and extend the chat and session model to support multiple diagrams and rule packs per chat, grouped under projects:

1. A wider, labeled sidebar (icon + text, synara/MikeOSS-inspired) replaces the narrow icon-only rail and its flyout overlays. Sidebar items are real Next.js routes (`/assistant`, `/projects`, `/projects/[id]`, `/rule-packs`, `/rule-packs/[id]`) rather than a client-side view switch, per ADR 0006. The chat+P&ID review surface becomes one destination ("Assistant") among several, not the app's only surface.
2. A `review project` becomes concrete: a workspace that groups multiple chats. The distinction between a chat and a project is exactly this grouping — a project has multiple chats; a chat is not itself scoped to one project's diagram.
3. A `chat` becomes multi-document and multi-rule-pack: any chat (inside or outside a project) may have zero or more single-file review sessions and zero or more rule packs attached, each surfaced as a removable chip above the composer (MikeOSS-style). A request that addresses more than one attached diagram fans out to each diagram's own scoped execution (the existing restricted grounded-QA harness, parameterized by session) and combines the separate results in the model's prose answer — attached sessions' fact bases, predicate contracts, and evidence trails are never merged into a single cross-diagram traversal.
4. Every panel (sidebar, chat column, P&ID panel) becomes resizable and collapsible via `react-resizable-panels`. On desktop, collapsing the sidebar fully hides it (main content expands, a small toggle button reopens it); shrinking to an icon-only mini-rail is a narrow-viewport fallback only, not the desktop collapse behavior.
5. The static P&ID schematic SVG gets pan/zoom via `react-zoom-pan-pinch`, wrapping the existing render output without changing `schematic-scene-view.tsx`'s render logic.
6. Rule packs get a standalone browse page (`/rule-packs`, read-only reference, searchable table, no session required) plus an in-chat attach modal (search list + detail pane + View Page/Cancel/Use actions, mirroring MikeOSS's "Select workflow" modal) for actually loading a pack onto the active chat.
7. New icons replace the mismatched ones: `Layers` for Rule Packs (was `SlidersHorizontal`), `Inbox` for session history (was `Clock`). In the narrow-viewport icon-only fallback, the history item is dropped entirely (Assistant/Projects/Rule Packs remain); recent sessions become reachable via the expanded "Recent Projects" nav tree instead.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to zoom and pan the P&ID schematic, so that I can inspect a dense area of my own drawing without it staying fixed at a whole-drawing scale.
2. As a process engineer, I want to resize the chat column against the P&ID panel, so that I can give more room to whichever I'm focused on.
3. As a process engineer, I want to collapse the sidebar entirely when I want maximum space for the chat and drawing, and bring it back with one click.
4. As a process engineer, I want a Projects section, so that I can group my review work across multiple P&IDs, PFDs, or other diagrams instead of losing track of separate one-off chats.
5. As a process engineer, I want to attach more than one diagram to a single chat, so that I can ask a question like "what's downstream of the pump" and get an answer for each attached diagram without opening a separate chat per file.
6. As a process engineer, I want to attach more than one rule pack to a chat, so that I can combine e.g. a HAZOP-style pack with an internal-standard pack in one review session.
7. As a process engineer, I want each attached diagram and rule pack to show as a small removable chip above where I type, so that I always see what's currently in scope for my question.
8. As a process engineer, I want a standalone page where I can browse and search all rule packs and read their rules' plain-language restatements, so that I can evaluate what's available without needing an active chat.
9. As a process engineer, I want a focused modal for actually loading a rule pack onto my chat — searchable list, detail pane, and clear View Page/Cancel/Use actions — so that attaching a pack is a deliberate, reviewable step.
10. As a process engineer, I want the Rule Pack nav icon to actually look like a pack of something, and the session-history icon to not be a clock, so that the sidebar's purpose is legible at a glance.
11. As a process engineer, I want the sidebar to show my recent projects with their chats nested underneath, so that I can navigate back into ongoing review work the way I would in any other project-based tool.
12. As a process engineer, I want the app's URLs to reflect where I am (a specific project, a specific rule pack), so that the browser back button and bookmarking work the way they do everywhere else.
13. As a maintainer, I want the schematic pan/zoom added without touching the backend-owned scene computation (ADR 0005), so that the trust boundary between geometry decisions and rendering stays intact.
14. As a maintainer, I want multi-diagram fan-out to reuse the existing restricted grounded-QA harness (parameterized by session) rather than a new execution path, so that per-session predicate contracts, evidence trails, and audit records stay unchanged in shape.
15. As a maintainer, I want the new page-navigated shell to reuse `react-resizable-panels` and `react-zoom-pan-pinch` rather than hand-rolled drag/zoom math, so that resize/zoom edge cases (min/max size, zoom-to-cursor) aren't reimplemented and re-debugged in this repo.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Navigation**: replace the narrow icon-rail + flyout-overlay app shell with a wider icon+label sidebar navigating real Next.js App Router routes: `/assistant` (default chat, no project), `/projects` (list), `/projects/[id]` (one project: nested chats + P&ID), `/rule-packs` (searchable table), `/rule-packs/[id]` (detail). See ADR 0006.
- **Domain model** (glossary updated in `CONTEXT.md`): `review project` = a workspace grouping multiple chats. `chat` = a conversation thread that may have zero or more single-file review sessions and zero or more rule packs attached; the project/chat distinction is exactly the grouping, not multi-document capability, which belongs to the chat itself. `single-file review session` keeps its one-file boundary (fact base, predicate contract, evidence trail never merged across sessions) — the one-file boundary is per session, not per chat.
- **Fan-out execution**: a chat request addressing multiple attached sessions is answered by the existing restricted grounded-QA harness, with its tools parameterized by session identifier so the model selects which attached session's tool to call per sub-question (extends `model-planned topology retrieval`, not a new mechanism). The model composes one prose answer referencing results from each session; no cross-session join or merged traversal is introduced.
- **Sidebar collapse semantics**: desktop collapse = sidebar fully hidden, main content expands, small toggle button reopens it. Icon-only mini-rail is a narrow-viewport/mobile fallback only. In that fallback, the session-history nav item is omitted entirely (Assistant/Projects/Rule Packs remain); recent sessions are reached via the expanded "Recent Projects" tree instead.
- **Rule pack UX split**: `/rule-packs` is a standalone, session-independent browse/reference table. Actually loading a pack onto the active chat stays a modal launched from the chat (search list + detail pane + View Page/Cancel/Use actions, mirroring MikeOSS's "Select workflow" modal) since loading/running is inherently chat-scoped. Multiple packs may be attached to one chat simultaneously; each gets its own removable chip.
- **Diagram attach**: symmetric with rule-pack attach — a "+ Documents"-style composer trigger opens an attach flow; each attached diagram gets its own removable chip.
- **Panel resize**: `react-resizable-panels` for the sidebar/chat/P&ID three-panel layout — drag-resize, min/max constraints, collapse-to-hidden, keyboard resize.
- **P&ID pan/zoom**: `react-zoom-pan-pinch` wraps the existing static SVG output of `schematic-scene-view.tsx` (wheel-zoom, drag-pan, pinch-zoom, reset-view) without changing that component's render logic. The Cytoscape-based topology-inspection debug view is unaffected — it already has its own zoom/pan.
- **Icons** (`lucide-react`, already a dependency): `Layers` for Rule Packs (was `SlidersHorizontal`), `Inbox` for session/chat history (was `Clock`).
- **New ADR**: `docs/adr/0006-page-navigated-app-shell.md` records the flyout-to-routed-pages shift and its trade-offs.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert external, observable behavior at the highest available seam — no assertions on component internals or pixels, consistent with this repo's existing convention (see the 2ki epic's testing decisions).
- **Backend seam (FastAPI `TestClient`)**: new chat-to-session and chat-to-rule-pack attach/detach endpoints; the restricted grounded-QA harness extended so its tools accept a session identifier, tested by preparing 2+ real fixtures under one chat and asserting fan-out tool calls resolve against the correct session each, with the final answer referencing evidence from both. Prior art: existing session-prepare and rule-pack-run TestClient tests.
- **Frontend `lib` seam (vitest)**: attachment-chip state and session/rule-pack list client functions, in the style of the existing `rule-pack-run.ts` / scene-client tests.
- **Playwright (scripted zero-LLM provider, extending `review-workflow.spec.ts` and `rule-pack-picker.spec.ts`)**: the new routed pages (`/projects`, `/rule-packs`) render and navigate correctly; the attach-modal + chip flow for both diagrams and rule packs; multi-pack attach (two chips, both packs' rules runnable); panel resize and collapse/reopen; P&ID pan/zoom interaction. Per prior discussion, resize/zoom and navigation are folded into the existing spec style rather than given a separate dedicated spec file.
- Visual quality remains explicitly not machine-tested — judged by the user against the design references, no screenshot diffing, consistent with the 2ki epic.
- **Known blocker to resolve before relying on Playwright signal**: per the prior session's handoff, the full Playwright suite was failing near-universally in that sandbox (composer Send button stuck disabled, likely tied to a failing Next.js dev-server HMR websocket) — this needs to be root-caused (the `diagnose` skill) before Playwright results here can be trusted; until then, lean on backend `TestClient` + frontend unit tests + manual verification, per that handoff's guidance.

## Out of Scope

- True cross-diagram reasoning that joins or merges two diagrams' fact bases into a single traversal (e.g. "trace this line across sheets" as one fused graph query) — fan-out stays per-session, combined only at the prose-answer level.
- User-uploaded rule packs, rule synthesis, and promotion (remains the future paid rule-authoring tier per glossary).
- Any change to the backend-owned schematic scene computation itself (ADR 0005) — pan/zoom is a pure rendering/interaction addition on top of the existing scene output.
- Account/auth system work beyond whatever minimal identity is needed to persist a project — this PRD assumes projects are persisted per the existing session-persistence mechanism, not a new auth system.
- Mobile-specific layout beyond the icon-only sidebar fallback already described.
- Root-causing the pre-existing Playwright composer-disabled regression itself (tracked separately; this PRD only depends on it being fixed for its own Playwright coverage to be trustworthy).

## Further Notes

- Glossary terms revised/introduced this round (see `CONTEXT.md`): `review project` (revised from "future" to concrete), `chat` (new, replaces the a since-abandoned `diagram-scoped chat`/`project-level chat` split), `single-file review session` (revised to decouple the one-file boundary from the chat).
- Governing ADRs: 0006 (page-navigated app shell, new this round), alongside 0004/0005 (schematic rendering, unaffected by this PRD except for the added pan/zoom wrapper) and 0002 (deterministic boundaries, which the fan-out execution model continues to honor).
- Design references: MikeOSS Workflows page + "Select workflow" modal + composer attachment chips; synara's project-containing-threads nav grouping; the current app's existing rule-pack-picker flyout as a UX pattern that mostly works and is being relocated/extended rather than redesigned from scratch.
- This was scoped via a `/grill-with-docs` session; several branches were resolved in sequence (project shape, cross-diagram scope, chat/project distinction, panel/zoom libraries, sidebar model, collapse semantics, rule-pack page split, icon choices) — see conversation history for the reasoning behind each, not duplicated here.

react-resizable-panels for the sidebar/chat/P&ID three-panel layout. react-zoom-pan-pinch wraps the existing static SVG schematic scene render for pan/zoom, without changing the scene's render logic or the backend-owned schematic scene computation (ADR 0005). comments.author: Vekram1
comments.text: HITL design references (2026-07-08, MikeOSS 'Add workflow' modal): composer has a labeled 'Rule Packs' trigger button (Mike: '+ Documents / Workflows / Projects' row inside the chat box). title: PRD: Schematic review experience — tiered renderer, calm shell, stepped turns, rule-pack picker
description:
## Problem Statement

A process engineer uploads a DEXPI P&ID and gets a review experience that undermines the product's own trust story. The topology review view is an abstract node cloud that discards the visual language engineers read fluently, so evidence highlighting points at bubbles instead of the drawing they are reviewing. Assistant turns render as a single prose blob with clunky tool dumps, so the user cannot see what the system did, what it checked, or where it paused for their judgment. Bundled rule packs — the product's exhaustiveness story — have no user-facing surface at all. The current frontend (post-worktree) is functionally correct but visually unrefined, and the earlier polished frontend lacks the new turn lifecycle behavior. Meanwhile, real-world DEXPI exports carry full drawing geometry that the product ignores.

## Solution

Rebuild the presentation layer around four pillars, on top of the merged backend:

1. A tiered topology review view: a drawing-faithful schematic view rendered from the source file's own geometry and file-defined symbol shapes when the geometry sanity gate passes, degrading honestly — inferred pipe routing per element, an unplaced-equipment shelf for unpositioned equipment, and a full auto-layout schematic view when the gate fails. Every inference is disclosed in a typed geometry report; the abstract graph survives only as a debug topology-inspection view.
2. A backend-owned schematic scene: all symbol resolution, routing, gating, shelf, and disclosure decisions are computed during session preparation in the same codebase that parses the source; the frontend paints and handles interaction only (ADR 0005).
3. A calm, MikeOSS-inspired shell: white ground, serif display face for brand moments, shadow-based elevation, sidebar navigation (Assistant / Rule Packs / Sessions), hero input, with stepped turn presentation — assistant turns render as ordered step rows derived from turn lifecycle events, with disclosure dropdowns, inline blocking review cards (Datalog consent, direction review), and the grounded answer as the final block.
4. A rule-pack picker: searchable pack list with a restatement-first detail pane, load-on-select, run-as-primary-action, and in-thread rule results as stepped turns with evaluation outcomes and evidence chips.

Precondition: merge the worktree branch (turn lifecycle, server-owned Datalog proposals, audit records, consent card semantics) into main, preserving main's prior UI polish as a checkpoint commit for reference only.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want my uploaded P&ID rendered as the drawing I recognize — pumps as pump symbols, vessels as vessels, pipes as orthogonal runs — so that reviewing the model feels like reviewing my drawing, not a database.
2. As a process engineer, I want the schematic rendered from the geometry my CAD tool exported, so that positions and pipe runs match the original drawing rather than an invented layout.
3. As a process engineer, I want equipment symbols drawn from the file's own shape catalogue when present, so that the rendering matches my organization's drawing conventions.
4. As a process engineer, I want a familiar ISO-style symbol substituted when the file provides no shape, so that gaps never render as meaningless boxes.
5. As a process engineer, I want pipes with missing centerline geometry auto-routed between their true endpoints and visibly marked as inferred, so that I can see complete connectivity without being misled about what was drawn.
6. As a process engineer, I want equipment that has no position in the file shown on a clearly separate shelf beside the drawing with leader lines to its connections, so that I can see the whole plant without the drawing frame lying about placement.
7. As a process engineer, I want a file whose geometry is mostly missing or degenerate presented as a clearly-labeled auto-layout schematic rather than a half-real mixture, so that I always know which fidelity level I am looking at.
8. As a process engineer, I want a geometry health summary when my file is prepared — what was placed as drawn, what was inferred, what was demoted and why — so that I can calibrate my trust before asking questions.
9. As a process engineer, I want to click any object in the schematic and see its identity, attributes, and connections, so that inspection starts from the drawing.
10. As a process engineer, I want answer evidence highlighted directly on the schematic — including shelved and inferred elements — so that claims point at the drawing I am reviewing.
11. As a process engineer, I want evidence highlighting to auto-open the schematic panel when an answer references objects, so that I never miss what an answer is grounded in.
12. As a process engineer, I want the schematic panel collapsible and reopenable across the upload lifecycle, so that I control my workspace.
13. As a process engineer, I want a debug topology-inspection view still available, so that I can inspect raw extracted nodes and edges when something looks wrong.
14. As a process engineer, I want each assistant turn shown as a sequence of step rows — what was retrieved, what was validated, what was executed — so that I can see how the answer was produced at a glance.
15. As a process engineer, I want each step row expandable to its details (arguments, evidence rows, diagnostics), so that I can audit any step without wading through all of them.
16. As a process engineer, I want required reviews — Datalog consent, direction review — to appear inline in the step sequence as blocking steps, so that approval moments are first-class and in context.
17. As a process engineer, I want the Datalog consent card to keep its interpretation, scope, assumptions, exact-Datalog disclosure, and effect statement in the new presentation, so that execution consent stays informed.
18. As a process engineer, I want the grounded answer as the final block of the turn with claim-level evidence chips, so that conclusions stay connected to their witnesses.
19. As a process engineer, I want a Rule Packs section in the navigation, so that the product's bundled checks are discoverable instead of hidden.
20. As a process engineer, I want to search and browse bundled rule packs with each rule shown as its engineer-readable restatement first, so that I can judge what a pack checks without reading Datalog.
21. As a process engineer, I want the executable Datalog of a bundled rule available behind a disclosure, so that I can inspect the logic when I choose to.
22. As a process engineer, I want selecting a pack to load it into my active session, so that standards reasoning has an explicit grounding source.
23. As a process engineer, I want a Run-all-checks action on a loaded pack and per-rule run actions, so that evaluation is an explicit choice, never a side effect of browsing.
24. As a process engineer, I want rule results delivered in the chat thread as a stepped turn — one step per rule with satisfied/violated/indeterminate outcome and evidence — so that the conversation remains the single narrative of my review session.
25. As a process engineer, I want violated and indeterminate outcomes to carry their evidence and limitations, so that absence of proof is never presented as compliance.
26. As a process engineer, I want a calm, uncluttered shell — white ground, quiet chrome, generous space — so that a long review session does not fatigue me.
27. As a process engineer, I want a hero input on the empty state inviting a question about my document, so that starting a session is obvious.
28. As a process engineer, I want sidebar navigation for Assistant, Rule Packs, and Sessions, so that the product's surfaces are legible from anywhere.
29. As a returning user, I want my recent sessions listed in the sidebar, so that I can resume a review within the product's session-retention rules.
30. As a process engineer, I want the app to state that answers are grounded in the uploaded drawing as-is, so that the boundary between document truth and field truth stays explicit.
31. As a maintainer, I want the schematic scene computed in the backend next to the parser, so that the geometry report and the render can never disagree.
32. As a maintainer, I want scene preparation covered by deterministic tests over the real-world fixtures (C01, C02, C03) and geometry-free fixtures (E-series), so that fidelity decisions are regression-protected without a browser.
33. As a maintainer, I want the e2e suite to keep running against the scripted zero-LLM provider, so that presentation changes are verified deterministically and cheaply.
34. As a maintainer, I want the worktree's turn lifecycle, server-owned proposal, and audit behavior merged into main unchanged, so that the rebuild sits on the reviewed security fixes.
35. As a maintainer, I want main's previous UI polish preserved in a checkpoint commit, so that the rebuild can reference it without hand-merging superseded components.

## Implementation Decisions

- Merge precedes all feature work: commit main's uncommitted frontend polish as a checkpoint, merge the worktree branch favoring branch behavior in conflicted presentation files, reinstall frontend dependencies to settle the lockfile, then verify with the full backend suite, frontend unit suite, and Playwright.
- The topology review view is tiered per ADR 0004: drawing-faithful schematic view when the geometry sanity gate passes; auto-layout schematic view otherwise; topology-inspection view demoted to debug. Source positions are never mixed with invented in-frame positions.
- Geometry sanity gate: requires non-degenerate drawing extent, pipe-geometry coverage above a calibrated threshold, and unpositioned-equipment share below a calibrated threshold. Thresholds are calibrated during the renderer spike, not fixed in advance.
- Per-element demotion applies only to pipe routing (inferred pipe routing between true endpoints, one uniform inferred-style cue) and to unpositioned equipment (unplaced-equipment shelf outside the drawing frame with leader lines and disclosure). Equipment positions are all-or-nothing within the frame.
- Symbol resolution order: file-defined symbol shape first, bundled symbol library second, generic labeled placeholder last. The bundled symbol library is repository-owned, ISO 10628-styled, keyed by DEXPI component class, and also serves all auto-layout rendering.
- The schematic scene is backend-owned per ADR 0005: session preparation emits a renderer-agnostic scene (placed symbols, polylines, labels, inferred-style cues, object identities for hit-testing) plus the typed geometry report. The frontend is a painter and interaction layer only. Tier-2 layout computation may execute client-side if the spike favors a JavaScript layout engine, but the decision to auto-layout and its disclosure remain backend-owned.
- The geometry report is the single source of truth: renderer decisions and the user-facing health summary read the same typed diagnostics. The report describes and demotes but never repairs source geometry in OSS v1.
- The chat runtime (assistant-ui runtime and thread state) is retained; the entire turn body renderer is rebuilt as stepped turn presentation mapping turn lifecycle events to step rows. If the message abstraction resists the step model, the thread view is swapped while keeping the runtime.
- Stepped turn presentation renders required human reviews (logic-request confirmation card, direction review card) inline as blocking steps; the evidence-linked natural-language answer is the final block with claim-level evidence chips.
- Streaming of grounded agent turns is promoted to core UX and sequenced immediately after the shell, since step rows only tick live once turns stream.
- The rule-pack picker follows load-on-select plus run-as-primary-action semantics, with a restatement-first detail pane and collapsed executable logic, honoring bundled rule-pack trust (no per-session confirmation for bundled rules). Rule evaluation results arrive as in-thread rule results.
- Shell design language: white ground, one serif display face for brand moments, quiet gray sans chrome, shadow-based elevation, one accent color; sidebar navigation Assistant / Rule Packs / Sessions; hero input empty state.
- Execution order: merge, then renderer spike (C01/C02/C03 to scene to SVG; decides layout engine, validates scene schema, calibrates gate thresholds), then shell prototype with fake data judged by the user's eyes, then re-cut of the open 21-series beads against this PRD.
- Vision-based ingestion of image P&IDs is explicitly rejected for now; the product stays DEXPI-native and positions digitization tools as upstream suppliers.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert external behavior at the highest available seam; no assertions on private helpers, component internals, or pixels.
- Schematic scene and geometry report: tested at the existing FastAPI TestClient boundary by preparing real fixtures. C01 asserts file-shape symbol resolution and as-drawn placement; C02/C03 exercise middling and sparse geometry; E-series fixtures assert auto-layout demotion; targeted fixtures assert inferred pipe routing flags, shelf membership, and typed diagnostic codes. Prior art: the existing session-prepare and temporary-Datalog review tests.
- Frontend logic: vitest at the lib seam for the scene client and scene-to-SVG mapping, following the existing review-backend and turn-client test style.
- User-visible behavior: Playwright against the scripted zero-LLM provider — stepped turn rows with disclosure, inline blocking consent card, rule-pack load-on-select and in-thread results, schematic hit-testable objects, evidence highlighting targets, shelf and inferred-pipe cues on a geometry-poor fixture. Prior art: the existing review-workflow spec.
- Visual quality is explicitly not machine-tested; it is judged by the user against the design references. No screenshot diffing.
- The merge is verified by the full pre-existing suites passing unchanged plus a manual pass of the real app.

## Out of Scope

- Vision-model ingestion of image P&IDs or PFDs, and any extraction pipeline for non-DEXPI inputs.
- Geometry repair (coordinate snapping, overlap fixing) — future work gated on repair-with-provenance.
- Field/as-built reconciliation features (walkdown notes, redline annotations).
- Automatic re-proposal for the consent card's revise actions (revise remains guidance to send a corrective message).
- User-uploaded rule packs, rule synthesis, and promotion (paid rule-authoring tier per glossary).
- Multi-file sessions, review projects, and account persistence beyond existing session behavior.
- Certified-drawing claims of any kind; the rendering never substitutes for the stamped drawing.

## Further Notes

- Glossary terms introduced for this direction: drawing-faithful schematic view, auto-layout schematic view, topology-inspection view, file-defined symbol shape, bundled symbol library, symbol resolution order, geometry sanity gate, unplaced-equipment shelf, inferred pipe routing, geometry report, schematic scene, stepped turn presentation, rule-pack picker, in-thread rule results.
- Governing ADRs: 0004 (render source geometry when present — reverses the earlier avoid-layout-faithful stance), 0005 (backend-owned schematic scene), alongside 0002 (deterministic boundaries).
- The renderer spike and shell prototype are throwaway; their output is decisions (layout engine, scene schema validation, gate thresholds, design direction), not shipped code.
- Design references: MikeOSS chat shell and workflow picker; Claude Code / Codex HITL step sequencing; the DEXPI C01 reference drawing as the fidelity bar.

title: Stepped turn presentation with inline blocking review cards
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki

## What to build

Rebuild the turn body renderer as stepped turn presentation: turn lifecycle events map to ordered step rows (retrieval, validation, execution, evidence) with status glyphs and expandable detail; the logic-request confirmation card and direction review card appear inline as blocking steps; the evidence-linked natural-language answer is the final block with claim-level evidence chips. Consent card content (interpretation, scope, assumptions, exact Datalog behind disclosure, effect statement, four actions) is preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A multi-step scripted turn renders as ordered step rows with per-step disclosure
- [ ] Datalog confirmation renders inline as a blocking step; turn resumes after decision
- [ ] Direction review card renders inline as a blocking step
- [ ] Final answer block carries evidence chips wired to schematic highlighting
- [ ] Consent card semantics unchanged (TestClient contract untouched; Playwright re-asserts card content)

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki.10
notes:
Rebuilt the turn body renderer as a stepped turn presentation, presentation-layer-only (runtime, turn-lifecycle backend, and the existing two-message-per-paused-turn model all unchanged).

New frontend/lib/turn-steps.ts: pure deriveTurnSteps(turn, reduced) synthesizes ordered step rows (retrieval, validation, evidence & answer) from the turn's existing coarse event log -- no fabricated sub-step detail, since the backend genuinely has none (confirmed via research: only tool-progress/text/evidence/review-required/terminal events exist; tool_call_trace is intentionally not exposed). Retrieval step reads the last tool-progress event (started vs resumed) so a resumed message's own step list is derived correctly. Validation step appears only when reduceTurn() returns review-required (blocked, with datalog-confirmation or direction-review detail kind); absent on resumed messages since completion wins the same precedence reduceTurn() already implements. 6 unit tests in turn-steps.test.ts cover all four real scenarios.

Extended DatalogConfirmationState/GroundedLogicAnswerState/DirectionReviewState/GroundedQAAnswerState with an optional steps?: TurnStep[] field (additive, backward compatible with the legacy non-turn-lifecycle review-backend.ts paths which produce no steps). turn-client.ts's turnToMessage() computes steps once via deriveTurnSteps and threads it into all four card-producing serializer calls.

New components/assistant-ui/stepped-turn-card.tsx: a thin wrapper (SteppedTurnCard) around the four existing card components -- does not re-implement their content, just renders an ordered step-row list with the last step's body slot holding the existing DatalogConfirmationCard/DirectionReviewCard/GroundedQAAnswerCard/GroundedLogicAnswerCard JSX verbatim. Zero testid/aria-label/button churn inside those four components. Renders nothing extra when steps is empty (legacy path).

globals.css: new .calm-step-card/.calm-step-row/.calm-step-glyph/.calm-step-label/.calm-step-body classes; re-themed .datalog-confirmation-card/.grounded-logic-answer-card/.datalog-consent-section onto calm tokens (2ki.10 had explicitly skipped these); added first-ever CSS for .direction-review-card/.grounded-qa-answer-card/.qa-evidence-chip* (previously zero rules, default browser styling only).

Playwright: augmented 4 existing tests in review-workflow.spec.ts with step-row assertions (no-pause has no validation step; datalog-confirmation and direction-review pauses show a blocked validation step; the resumed message has its own retrieval+evidence-answer step list with no validation step). Added one new dedicated test asserting step-row order directly, using a mocked paused-turn route (not a live E06 upload) since E06-fixture-based tests hit a pre-existing, already-confirmed-unrelated cytoscape-pid-graph upload issue (verified via git stash isolation earlier this session, present before any 2ki.10/2ki.11 work).

Verification: tsc clean, all 58 frontend unit tests pass (52 pre-existing + 6 new), full Playwright suite shows exactly 7 passed / 9 failed -- the 9 failures are byte-identical to the pre-existing baseline (8 unrelated E06/cytoscape failures + the known 2ki.6 inferred-cue flake) confirmed at the start of this session; the two tests that depend only on mocked routes (not live E06 upload) -- the Datalog confirmation test and the new stepped-rows test -- both pass with real signal, validating the blocking-step and resumed-step-list behavior end to end.

title: Stream grounded agent turns into stepped presentation
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Make step rows tick live: stream turn lifecycle events to the client as the turn executes so steps appear and complete in real time, pauses for blocking review appear the moment the backend pauses, and the final answer streams into the last block. Supersedes pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.21.17 (stream grounded agent turns in the web chat), promoted to core UX by the PRD.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Steps appear incrementally during an executing turn rather than all at once on completion
- [ ] A blocking review step appears as soon as the backend pauses the turn
- [ ] Cancellation mid-stream leaves the turn in the canceled state with the step trail intact
- [ ] Scripted-provider Playwright coverage exercises incremental appearance deterministically
- [ ] No regression in turn lifecycle persistence semantics

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki.11
notes:
Implemented streamed turn presentation, entirely via existing infrastructure -
no new backend endpoints needed. Key research finding: TurnLifecycleStore.begin()
already persists the turn to disk before execute() runs synchronously in the
POST /turns request thread, and computeTurnId() already lets the frontend know
the deterministic turn_id before that POST resolves. So the frontend can poll
GET /turns/{turnId} concurrently with the outstanding POST and observe active
-> paused/completed/canceled/failed transitions live, with zero new backend
transport (the half-built, unused GET .../turns/{turnId}/events NDJSON endpoint
was left untouched -- confirmed still dead code).

Frontend:
- turn-client.ts: reduceTurn() gains an explicit "in-progress" kind for an
  active turn with no terminal event yet (previously fell through to
  "answered" by accident, never exercised).
- turn-steps.ts: deriveTurnSteps() handles "in-progress" by returning a single
  {id: "retrieval", status: "pending"} row -- reuses the existing 3-step
  vocabulary (retrieval/validation/evidence-answer) rather than inventing
  per-tool-call granularity, since bead 2ki.11's tests hard-assert that
  collapsed vocabulary.
- New lib/in-progress-turn.ts: serializeInProgressTurn/parseInProgressTurnMessage,
  same tagged-JSON-string convention as grounded-qa-answer.ts. Wired into
  thread.tsx as a new SteppedTurnCard branch (last, before the MarkdownText
  fallback).
- pid-runtime-provider.tsx: modelAdapter.run converted from async function to
  async function* (AsyncGenerator<ChatModelRunResult, void> is a supported
  ChatModelAdapter.run return type). Polls getTurn every ~250ms, racing it
  against the original startPromise so callers that only mock the POST/cancel
  endpoints (most existing Playwright tests) still terminate correctly even
  though GET is never mocked.

Important discovered constraint (not in the original plan): assistant-ui's
LocalThreadRuntime discards any yielded content once it observes
abortSignal.aborted, marking the message "incomplete/cancelled" itself instead
(local-thread-runtime-core.js's for-await loop). This means a custom "The turn
was canceled." text is NOT deliverable through generator yields post-abort --
confirmed empirically (a debug run showed our correctly-computed canceled
content silently discarded). Revised the pre-existing bead-2ki.11-era
cancellation test's assertion to match this framework-native behavior instead
of custom text: composer returns to idle, no error, step trail left exactly as
it last stood. This arguably satisfies the AC's literal wording ("leaves the
turn in the canceled state with the step trail intact") better than the old
custom-text approach did.

Backend (test-determinism only, zero prod behavior change):
- ScriptedQATurnProvider gains step_delay_seconds (default 0.0, only sleeps if
  truthy) so Playwright can deterministically observe the turn mid-flight
  against the REAL scripted backend rather than a route mock.
- review_api.py's _resolve_qa_provider reads PYDEXPI_QA_SCRIPTED_STEP_DELAY_MS
  (default unset -> 0) when force_scripted.
- playwright.config.ts sets it to 300ms for the e2e backend only.

New Playwright tests (real scripted backend, not route mocks): a pending step
row ticks in before the final answer lands; canceling mid-stream leaves the
composer idle with the step trail frozen and no error. Also fixed one
pre-existing test whose sendPrompt() text I'd accidentally clobbered via an
overly broad sed during editing (restored to its original working prompt).

Verification: npx tsc --noEmit clean; node --test 62/62 (4 new: reduceTurn
in-progress branch, deriveTurnSteps in-progress branch, in-progress-turn
serializer round-trip); Playwright review-workflow.spec.ts +
schematic-scene.spec.ts + rule-pack-picker.spec.ts -> 23/24 with --workers=1
(only the same pre-existing 2ki.6 inferred-cue flake seen all session,
confirmed unrelated); backend pytest tests/ -q -> 313/314 (one pre-existing
flake, test_paused_review_can_reconnect_resume_once_or_cancel, confirmed
identical failure on a stash of my backend changes reverted -- not caused by
this bead).

title: Rule-pack backend: list, load, and run with demo pack
description:

- [ ] Load endpoint attaches a pack to the session; unloaded-standard responses unaffected for unloaded packs

- [ ] Demo pump discharge check produces satisfied, violated, and indeterminate outcomes across chosen fixtures
- [ ] TestClient coverage for list, load, run-all, run-one, and outcome evidence

## Blocked by

title: Bundled symbol library coverage for the fixture corpus
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki

## What to build

Extend the starter bundled symbol library to every DEXPI component class appearing in the supported fixture corpus, ISO 10628-styled, keyed by component class, applied via the symbol resolution order (file shape first, bundled second, generic placeholder last). Tier-2 renders and tier-1 gap-fills across the corpus stop falling through to generic placeholders except for genuinely unknown classes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every component class in the fixture corpus resolves to a bundled symbol when no file shape exists
- [ ] Generic placeholder only for classes absent from both file and library, recorded as a typed diagnostic
- [ ] Symbol resolution order asserted at the TestClient seam across representative fixtures
- [ ] Auto-layout renders of corpus fixtures visually reviewed once for symbol sanity

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki.5
notes:
Implemented per-DEXPI-component-class bundled symbol library with a real
file -> bundled -> generic resolution chain for both schematic tiers.

Backend:
- New pydexpi_datalog/workflow/bundled_symbols.py: BUNDLED_SYMBOLS dict keyed
  by raw DEXPI ComponentClass, covering all 9 equipment classes found across
  the 35-fixture corpus (CentrifugalPump, ReciprocatingPump,
  PlateHeatExchanger, TubularHeatExchanger, Tank, PressureVessel, Vessel,
  ProcessColumn, TaggedColumnSection), plus GENERIC_PLACEHOLDER. Entries are
  the same polyline/circle/arc/polygon primitive dicts tier-1 already emits
  from file geometry, so no renderer-side change was needed to paint them.
- Tier-1 (schematic_scene.py _emit_symbol/_resolve_shape_key): a file
  catalogue miss no longer silently drops the item. It now falls back to
  BUNDLED_SYMBOLS by class_name (merged into scene.catalogue under a
  synthetic "__bundled__:<class>" key, counted in a new
  items_with_bundled_shape report field), then to a generic placeholder
  ("__generic__" key) recorded as a typed diagnostic in a new
  report.generic_placeholders list ({topology_id, raw_id, class_name,
  reason: "unknown_component_class"}). Both new fields are threaded through
  geometry_gate.py's evaluate_geometry_gate into the API's geometry_report.
- Tier-2 (pid_view.py _build_units/build_pid_view): each unit resolves a
  symbol_key from the raw DEXPI class already available as node["label"]
  (kept raw for Datalog/semantics, per review_session.py) against
  BUNDLED_SYMBOLS, falling back to "generic". build_pid_view returns a new
  symbol_report.generic_placeholders list of the same shape, keyed by
  unit_id, populated whenever a unit resolves to generic.

Frontend:
- PidUnit gained a symbolKey field (types.ts), populated in
  review-backend.ts's readPidView from unit.symbol_key.
- auto-layout-catalogue.ts was rekeyed from the old 7 coarse category
  buckets (pump/exchanger/vessel/column/valve/instrument/generic) to the 9
  exact DEXPI classes + generic, each with a distinct ISO-10628-styled
  primitive set. auto-layout-scene.ts now consumes unit.symbolKey directly
  instead of re-deriving a bucket from category+className
  (autoLayoutSymbolKeyFor removed). The Cytoscape topology-graph view
  (pid-symbols.ts) is a separate, earlier feature and was left untouched.

Tests:
- New tests/workflow/test_bundled_symbols.py: runs the real export pipeline
  across all 35 corpus fixtures and asserts every equipment class found is a
  BUNDLED_SYMBOLS key (encodes AC #1 directly).
- New BundledSymbolResolutionApiTests in tests/web/test_schematic_scene_api.py
  (TestClient seam, per AC #3): tier-1 catalogue-miss-with-known-class ->
  bundled fallback, no diagnostic; tier-1 catalogue-miss-with-unknown-class
  -> generic + typed diagnostic; tier-2 known-class corpus fixture (E06) ->
  no generic units; tier-2 unknown-class -> generic + typed diagnostic.
- New frontend/components/pid/auto-layout-catalogue.test.ts asserting
  catalogue coverage of all 9 classes + generic.

Verification:
- python -m pytest tests/ -q: 318/319 passing. The 1 failure
  (test_paused_review_can_reconnect_resume_once_or_cancel) is a
  long-documented pre-existing flake unrelated to this bead (previously
  confirmed via git-stash comparison in bead 2ki.12's closure).
- frontend: tsc --noEmit clean; node --test 63/63 passing.
- Full Playwright suite (review-workflow/schematic-scene/rule-pack-picker,
  --workers=1): converged to only pre-existing/order-dependent flakes across
  repeated runs (the long-standing 2ki.6 inferred-pipe-visibility flake, and
  two bead-2ki.12 tests with tight 250ms-poll-vs-300ms-scripted-delay timing
  margins) -- none touch symbol resolution. Directly verified the
  schematic-scene:53 (2ki.6) fixture (C03) against the real backend API:
  as-drawn scene, 15 symbols, 2 inferred pipes, 0 generic_placeholders,
  confirming tier-1 resolution is correct and the e2e flake is UI-timing,
  not a backend regression.
- AC #4 (visual review): browser-screenshot automation hit an unrelated
  Playwright file-chooser flake in this sandbox when run as an ad hoc single
  spec, so this was verified instead via direct topology API calls against
  E06 (CentrifugalPump, PlateHeatExchanger) and E07 (PressureVessel,
  TaggedColumnSection x2) -- all resolved to their correct per-class
  symbol_key with zero generic_placeholders -- plus printing the resolved
  primitive shapes for 4 classes to confirm they are visually distinct
  (circle+impeller pump, box+baffles reciprocating pump, circle+zigzag
  exchanger, capsule+heads pressure vessel, etc).
- Also discovered and resolved (unrelated to this bead's code): a corrupted
  stale .next build cache from repeated manual dev-server restarts this
  session was causing the composer's Send button to stay disabled; clearing
  .next resolved it, confirming it was environmental, not a regression.

title: Renderer spike: DEXPI geometry to schematic scene to SVG (throwaway)
description:

description:

title: Geometry sanity gate and tier-2 auto-layout schematic view
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki

## What to build

The honest degradation path. Backend evaluates the geometry sanity gate (non-degenerate extent, centerline coverage threshold, unpositioned-equipment share threshold from the spike). Files failing the gate get an auto-layout schematic scene: exact source connectivity, positions computed by the chosen layout engine, rendered with a starter bundled symbol library (pump, vessel, heat exchanger, valve, instrument bubble, nozzle), visibly labeled auto-layout. Positions from source are never mixed with invented in-frame positions. Preparing a geometry-free E-series fixture demos it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Gate outcome computed backend-side and recorded in the geometry report with typed diagnostics
- [ ] E-series fixture produces an auto-layout scene with bundled symbols and orthogonal-style presentation
- [ ] Auto-layout labeling visible in the UI; as-drawn claim absent
- [ ] If layout computes client-side, the decision to auto-layout and its disclosure remain backend-owned
- [ ] TestClient assertions for gate pass and fail across fixtures

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki.4
notes:
Implemented backend geometry sanity gate + frontend tier-2 auto-layout schematic view.

Backend (pydexpi_datalog/workflow/geometry_gate.py, new):
- evaluate_geometry_gate(scene) computes 3 typed metrics from the existing
  schematic_scene report + extent: degenerate extent (<10mm either dim,
  unit-normalized), pipe centerline coverage (<50% of segments, vacuous pass
  when segments==0), unpositioned equipment share (>20%, vacuous pass when
  no positionable equipment). Thresholds from renderer-spike NOTES.md sec 4.
- schematic_scene.py: split build_schematic_scene (existing None-filtering
  contract, unchanged) from new build_schematic_scene_report (always returns
  the raw scene+report, used by the gate) and exported has_drawable_geometry.
- review_session.py: computes geometry_report every prepare, and only ever
  discloses a scene as "as-drawn" when has_drawable_geometry AND the gate
  passes. Gate failure (or no geometry at all) sets schematic_scene=None and
  schematic_scene_kind="auto-layout" -- source positions are never mixed
  with invented ones (dropped entirely, not partially disclosed).
  "none" kind only when there's no DEXPI source path at all.
- topology_view now carries schematic_scene_kind ("as-drawn"|"auto-layout"|
  "none") and geometry_report, surfaced through chainlit_review_flow.py's
  topology_panel_state and the /prepare response (both backend-owned per
  ADR 0005, independent of where layout math later executes).
- Tests: tests/workflow/test_geometry_gate.py (9 unit cases: pass/fail per
  metric, vacuous-pass cases, unit normalization). tests/web/
  test_schematic_scene_api.py: added GeometrySanityGateApiTests with
  TestClient assertions for C01 (passes, as-drawn) and E06 (fails, degrades
  to auto-layout, pid_view connectivity still present) -- E06 is the
  standing E-series geometry-free fixture already used elsewhere.

Frontend (elkjs added as a dependency):
- components/pid/auto-layout-catalogue.ts: starter bundled symbol library
  (pump, vessel/tank, column, heat exchanger, valve, instrument, nozzle,
  generic) as SchematicScene primitives, reusing the existing
  symbolKeyFor() classification heuristic from pid-symbols.ts.
- components/pid/auto-layout-scene.ts: buildAutoLayoutScene(pidView) uses
  elkjs (layered algorithm, ORTHOGONAL edge routing, per the spike's
  decision) to compute positions for pid_view's exact source connectivity,
  emits a real SchematicScene (dashed "inferred routing" polylines, AUTO-
  LAYOUT frame text) reusing the existing SchematicSceneView renderer
  verbatim -- no new rendering code, no as-drawn claim anywhere.
- components/pid/auto-layout-scene-view.tsx: wraps the above with a visible
  "Auto-layout -- positions inferred, not as drawn" badge (dashed-border
  wrap, distinct styling from the as-drawn tier-1 wrap).
- graph-panel.tsx: new branch -- schematicScene present -> as-drawn (tier 1,
  unchanged); else schematicSceneKind==="auto-layout" && pidView non-empty
  -> new AutoLayoutSchematicView (tier 2); else falls through to the
  existing Cytoscape debug graph (kept for the "none"/legacy-source edge
  case) or the plain-SVG sample-graph demo state.
- types.ts / review-backend.ts / graph-context.tsx: threaded
  schematicSceneKind + geometryReport end to end.
- e2e/review-workflow.spec.ts: updated the two E06-based assertions that
  previously targeted "cytoscape-pid-graph" to target the new
  "auto-layout-schematic" testid (E06 now takes the tier-2 path instead of
  falling all the way to the debug graph) -- same data-highlight-active
  contract preserved.

Verification: backend tests/ 297 passed (1 pre-existing unrelated failure
in test_turn_lifecycle.py, reproduces identically on E06 direction-review
flow with no code path near this bead -- confirmed pre-existing, not caused
by this change). Frontend: tsc --noEmit clean, oxlint clean, npm test
52/52 passed. Playwright e2e could not be visually re-verified in this
session -- native file-chooser dialogs time out in this sandboxed browser
environment for every spec including untouched C01 tests, so this is an
environment limitation, not a regression; the two updated assertions are a

title: Inferred pipe routing with uniform disclosure cue
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-2ki

## What to build

Per-element demotion for pipes only. In a tier-1 scene, a pipe run whose source has no centerline geometry is routed between its true source-stated endpoints, drawn in the shared schematic visual language with the single uniform inferred-style cue, and recorded as a typed diagnostic in the geometry report. Equipment positions remain all-or-nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing-centerline pipe in an otherwise geometry-bearing fixture renders as a routed run between its real endpoints
- [ ] Exactly one uniform inferred-style cue distinguishes routed from drawn runs
- [ ] Geometry report carries a typed diagnostic per routed run
- [ ] Drawn runs are byte-identical to their scene geometry (no re-routing of good data)
- [ ] Playwright asserts the inferred cue on a geometry-poor fixture

## Blocked by
