title: PRD: Witness-grounded conversational P&ID QA
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers need to ask open-ended questions about an uploaded DEXPI source and receive useful natural-language answers without learning NetworkX, Datalog, or a domain-specific query language. The current workflow can prepare one source, generate and confirm Datalog, execute it, and return evidence, but it treats generated logic as the center of the backend. It does not yet provide a web-native model harness that can plan read-only topology retrieval, maintain conversational follow-ups, distinguish explicit from inferred engineering conclusions, or connect each answer claim to a complete structural witness.

The pyDEXPI full graph mirrors the source model and contains structural chains through nozzles, piping connections, piping nodes, network segments, equipment, and instrumentation. Simplifying those chains into a second engineering graph would hide information needed to justify topology answers and rule outcomes. A process-facing conclusion must therefore remain an interpretation of the pyDEXPI full graph and retain its complete structural path witness.

The product must also acknowledge inherent model risk. The application can constrain tools, execution, evidence, provenance, permissions, and confirmation, but it cannot guarantee model intelligence or prescribe every conversational response. The product needs a clear boundary where the model owns language interpretation, bounded retrieval planning, ambiguity handling, and prose while the backend owns deterministic evidence and execution controls.

## Solution

Build a witness-grounded, web-native QA harness over the existing pyDEXPI full graph. The application exposes constrained read-only topology and bundled-rule tools to native tool-capable models. The model chooses which tools to call, may perform a bounded sequence of retrievals, handles ambiguity conversationally, and writes a natural-language answer from returned evidence. The backend validates every tool call, applies resource and evidence budgets, preserves provenance, and streams typed conversation, turn, item, review, and completion events to the React frontend.

Keep the pyDEXPI full NetworkX graph as the only graph representation. Introduce a shared topology interpretation layer that computes process-facing relationships from raw paths and returns every conclusion with its complete ordered structural witness. Classify direction as explicit, inferred, or unknown. When inferred direction is necessary, let the user inspect the highlighted path and confirm, reverse, or mark the direction unknown through a session-scoped review annotation that never mutates source evidence.

Allow read-only retrieval and trusted repository-bundled rule execution to run immediately. Expose generated Datalog as a confirmation-required model capability used when read-only tools are insufficient. The generated query and engineer-readable restatement form one exact temporary query pair. Backend safety validation and explicit user confirmation are required before execution. Generated logic is never promoted into a reusable rule in OSS v1.

Return rule evaluations as justified satisfied, violated, or indeterminate outcomes. Every outcome includes evidence. Absence-based violations require a complete bounded evaluation scope and evidence explaining why traversal was complete. Apply claim-aware truncation so all grounded partial evidence is reported, while partial coverage never establishes a universal or absence conclusion.

Present answers as natural language with claim-level evidence chips. Selecting a chip opens the topology view, highlights the structural witness, and exposes evidence details. The model may provide useful chip labels, while backend metadata remains authoritative for provenance, direction, review status, and limitations.

OSS v1 permits one successfully prepared DEXPI XML source file per chat, not one guaranteed drawing page. Preparation is protected by configurable input, XML, graph, artifact, and execution resource limits. Pairwise comparison, multi-source projects, bulk checking, user-uploaded executable rule packs, policy-document ingestion, and reusable-rule authoring remain future workflows.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to ask questions in ordinary language, so that I do not need to learn NetworkX or Datalog syntax.
2. As a process engineer, I want the model to choose appropriate read-only topology tools, so that the conversation remains flexible.
3. As a process engineer, I want direct topology questions answered without Datalog confirmation, so that simple questions remain fast.
4. As a process engineer, I want explanatory questions answered from bounded topology evidence, so that explanations remain grounded.
5. As a process engineer, I want formal or recursive questions to escalate to generated Datalog when necessary, so that complex reasoning remains available.
6. As a process engineer, I want generated Datalog to require confirmation, so that model-proposed logic never executes silently.
7. As a process engineer, I want the generated query and engineer-readable restatement approved together, so that executable logic cannot drift from reviewed meaning.
8. As a process engineer, I want confirmation to mean execution consent for the current query, so that temporary questions are not mistaken for reusable rules.
9. As a process engineer, I want repository-bundled rules to execute immediately, so that trusted repeated checks do not require unnecessary confirmation.
10. As a process engineer, I want every process-facing relationship backed by its complete structural path, so that simplified conclusions remain auditable.
11. As a process engineer, I want nozzle, connection, segment, and piping-node evidence retained, so that required structural relationships are not hidden.
12. As a process engineer, I want explicit and inferred flow direction distinguished, so that assumptions are visible.
13. As a process engineer, I want unknown direction reported honestly, so that missing source information is not replaced with certainty.
14. As a process engineer, I want to inspect inferred direction in the graph, so that I can use engineering judgment.
15. As a process engineer, I want to confirm inferred direction, so that an otherwise indeterminate question can continue.
16. As a process engineer, I want to reverse an incorrect inferred direction, so that the answer uses my reviewed interpretation.
17. As a process engineer, I want to mark direction unknown, so that I am not forced into a false binary choice.
18. As a process engineer, I want reviewed direction stored only as a session annotation, so that source evidence remains unchanged.
19. As a process engineer, I want a direction annotation reused when the exact path and boundary are unchanged, so that I am not repeatedly asked the same question.
20. As a process engineer, I want changed paths or boundaries to invalidate prior direction review, so that stale judgments are not silently reused.
21. As a process engineer, I want ambiguous object references handled conversationally, so that the chat does not feel like a rigid form.
22. As a process engineer, I want answers for multiple plausible candidates when practical, so that ambiguity can still produce useful information.
23. As a process engineer, I want inferred object interpretation disclosed, so that I can correct the model naturally.
24. As a process engineer, I want follow-up questions to understand prior turns, so that I can say “what about the other pump?” or “why did you infer that?”
25. As a process engineer, I want prior evidence reusable by reference, so that follow-ups remain grounded without repeating the entire explanation.
26. As a process engineer, I want prior model prose treated only as conversation context, so that earlier unsupported wording never becomes engineering evidence.
27. As a process engineer, I want long conversations compacted without losing my decisions, so that follow-ups remain coherent.
28. As a process engineer, I want evidence identities, confirmations, annotations, and limitations preserved through compaction, so that provenance survives long chats.
29. As a process engineer, I want streamed responses and tool progress, so that the web chat remains responsive during multi-step work.
30. As a process engineer, I want paused review actions to survive refresh or reconnect, so that confirmation work is not lost.
31. As a process engineer, I want to cancel an active turn, so that I remain in control of long-running work.
32. As a process engineer, I want natural-language answers rather than raw JSON, so that results are readable.
33. As a process engineer, I want claim-level evidence chips, so that I can inspect why a specific statement was made.
34. As a process engineer, I want an evidence chip to open and highlight the supporting graph path, so that prose and topology remain connected.
35. As a process engineer, I want evidence chips to disclose inferred, explicit, user-confirmed, rule-scope, and limitation metadata, so that evidence types are not conflated.
36. As a process engineer, I want unfamiliar evidence types to remain inspectable, so that the answer does not fail because presentation metadata evolved.
37. As a process engineer, I want every rule outcome to be satisfied, violated, or indeterminate, so that “no finding” is not treated as proof.
38. As a process engineer, I want satisfied outcomes justified by matching evidence, so that passing results are auditable.
39. As a process engineer, I want absence-based violations justified by an exhaustively evaluated bounded scope, so that incomplete traversal is not called a violation.
40. As a process engineer, I want missing start, direction, termination, or completeness evidence to produce an indeterminate result, so that uncertainty remains explicit.
41. As a process engineer, I want all grounded partial evidence reported when limits are reached, so that useful work is not discarded.
42. As a process engineer, I want partial coverage prevented from proving universal or absence claims, so that truncation does not create false certainty.
43. As a process engineer, I want witnessed counterexamples to disprove universal claims when logically sufficient, so that valid negative evidence is still useful.
44. As a process engineer, I want general P&ID and process-engineering questions answered from model knowledge, so that the assistant remains educational.
45. As a process engineer, I want general-knowledge source posture disclosed, so that educational guidance is not confused with loaded-source evidence.
46. As a process engineer, I want source-specific calculations to disclose missing operating data, so that the model does not invent inputs.
47. As a process engineer, I want unrelated questions redirected toward P&ID work, so that the product remains focused without rigid topic forms.
48. As an OSS user, I want to select any native tool-capable model offered through my configured provider, so that I retain model choice.
49. As an OSS user, I want models without native tool calling disregarded, so that unsupported models do not enter a broken workflow.
50. As an OSS user, I do not want model quality scores or certification badges, so that the product does not imply guarantees it cannot make.
51. As an OSS user, I want runtime model capability failures shown clearly, so that provider or metadata drift is understandable.
52. As an OSS user, I want one DEXPI source file per chat, so that source and conversation scope remain clear.
53. As an OSS user, I want the system to accept a broad valid conceptual model without pretending it is one graphical page, so that DEXPI semantics are respected.
54. As an OSS user, I want oversized sources rejected with explicit resource diagnostics, so that preparation does not fail mysteriously.
55. As an OSS user, I want failed uploads retryable before a source is established, so that corrected input does not require restarting the app.
56. As an OSS user, I want bundled demo rule packs clearly labeled non-authoritative, so that examples are not mistaken for certified compliance logic.
57. As an OSS user, I want the pack mechanism to support multiple packs and rules, so that additional examples can be added without redesign.
58. As an OSS user, I want at least one complete pump discharge check-valve rule, so that the grounded rule workflow is demonstrable end to end.
59. As an OSS user, I do not want uploaded executable rule packs accepted in v1, so that ungoverned logic cannot become trusted.
60. As an OSS user, I do not want uploaded policy documents silently converted into rules, so that policy synthesis is not confused with trusted execution.
61. As a future CLI user, I want the CLI to consume the same backend run lifecycle, so that web and CLI answers use identical evidence boundaries.
62. As a developer, I want the pyDEXPI full graph to remain the only NetworkX graph, so that structural evidence is never lost through a second materialized graph.
63. As a developer, I want shared topology operations rather than consumer-specific traversal, so that NetworkX, Datalog, the model, and the frontend agree.
64. As a developer, I want source-qualified evidence identities, so that future multi-source projects do not require redesigning provenance.
65. As a developer, I want model planning separated from backend execution, so that conversational flexibility does not grant execution authority.
66. As a developer, I want application tools classified as allowed, confirmation-required, or denied, so that the model harness has an explicit permission boundary.
67. As a developer, I want arbitrary shell, filesystem, graph mutation, and unrestricted network tools unavailable, so that the harness remains domain-constrained.
68. As a developer, I want provider/model tool capability checked for the exact combination, so that provider-wide assumptions do not admit incompatible models.
69. As a developer, I want tool arguments and evidence references validated independently of model quality, so that application invariants remain deterministic.
70. As a developer, I want generated Datalog context limited to the predicate contract and relevant resolved identities, so that the full fact database is not sent by default.
71. As a developer, I want mechanical Datalog safety validation separated from semantic approval, so that backend guarantees remain honest.
72. As a developer, I want one server-owned conversation, turn, and item lifecycle, so that streaming, pause, resume, and future clients share a contract.
73. As a developer, I want idempotent resume and tool execution, so that reconnects do not duplicate work.
74. As a developer, I want resource and evidence budgets configurable, so that deployment limits can evolve without changing engineering semantics.
75. As a product owner, I want pairwise P&ID comparison treated as a separate future workflow, so that OSS v1 is not burdened with cross-source alignment.
76. As a product owner, I want bulk multi-source rule execution reserved for a future paid project workflow, so that OSS and paid capabilities have a meaningful boundary.
77. As a product owner, I want user rule-pack upload and policy-to-rule authoring reserved for a future paid tier, so that OSS v1 demonstrates rather than governs custom rules.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep the accepted Python backend API plus React/TypeScript frontend architecture.
- Keep the pyDEXPI full NetworkX graph as the sole graph representation.
- Persist canonical base facts as the stable, provenance-preserving serialization of the pyDEXPI full graph.
- Build a shared topology interpretation layer over the pyDEXPI full graph rather than a materialized engineering graph.
- Return complete ordered structural path witnesses for every process-facing relationship.
- Treat process-facing relationships as computed conclusions, not independent source facts.
- Classify flow direction as explicit, inferred, or unknown.
- Keep direction evidence status separate from user review status.
- Store user-confirmed, reversed, or unknown direction as a session annotation attached to an exact path witness and evaluation boundary.
- Invalidate direction annotations on new source, changed path, or changed boundary.
- Expose application-owned read-only topology tools and let the model plan their bounded use.
- Do not build a deterministic intent compiler, topic classifier, or mandatory ambiguity-selection UI.
- Support bounded multi-candidate retrieval so the model can answer for several plausible objects.
- Require native tool calls and tool-result continuation. Do not parse text-only pseudo-tool calls.
- Filter model availability by exact provider/model tool capability metadata, following the Models.dev pattern.
- Treat runtime provider rejection as authoritative when capability metadata is stale.
- Do not expose model quality scores, tested badges, certification tiers, or hardcoded family blacklists.
- Keep grounding evaluations as internal regression tests rather than product eligibility gates.
- Implement a restricted grounded-QA harness with allowed, confirmation-required, and denied tools.
- Deny arbitrary shell, filesystem mutation, graph mutation, and unrestricted network tools.
- Apply configurable per-operation and per-turn budgets for steps, time, paths, rows, evidence objects, path length, and payload size.
- Apply claim-aware truncation based on logical claim type rather than response wording.
- Report all grounded evidence obtained, coverage, and explicit limitations.
- Expose generated Datalog as a confirmation-required model capability.
- Supply generated-query context with the predicate contract, output contract, execution restrictions, conversation context, and relevant identities already resolved through retrieval.
- Do not send the complete session fact database to the model by default.
- Validate generated Datalog mechanically for approved predicates, output shape, append-only behavior, syntax, filesystem and include restrictions, size, timeout, and row limits.
- Pair generated Datalog with an engineer-readable restatement and confirm the exact pair.
- Treat confirmation as temporary execution consent, not reusable-rule promotion.
- Allow trusted repository-bundled rule-pack rules to execute immediately.
- Support multiple bundled packs and rules while requiring one complete pump discharge check-valve rule initially.
- Represent every rule evaluation as satisfied, violated, or indeterminate with evidence.
- Require scope-completeness evidence for absence-based violations.
- Treat model-only direction inference as insufficient for a formal rule outcome until user-reviewed.
- Build a server-owned review-session, conversation, turn, item, approval, interruption, and completion lifecycle inspired by Codex App Server concepts without depending on its runtime.
- Stream server events to the web frontend; keep tool execution and agent state out of browser code.
- Use server-to-browser event streaming plus ordinary HTTP review actions initially.
- Persist paused run state and make resume, cancellation, and tool execution idempotent.
- Preserve prior turns for conversational follow-ups.
- Preserve user decisions, resolved objects, evidence identities, confirmations, annotations, and limitations as structured conversation state.
- Compact older prose when necessary without promoting model prose into evidence.
- Accept free-form model answer text with references to known evidence IDs.
- Validate evidence references without prescribing prose.
- Render natural-language answers with claim-level evidence chips rather than raw response envelopes.
- Let the model supply useful chip labels while backend metadata controls provenance, direction, review status, trust, and limitations.
- Make evidence chips open the topology panel, highlight the exact structural witness, and display details.
- Allow general P&ID and process-engineering education from model knowledge with disclosed source posture.
- Require witnessed evidence for claims about the loaded source.
- Keep model-led domain redirection conversational rather than deterministic.
- Limit OSS v1 to one successfully prepared DEXPI XML source file per chat.
- Do not equate one source file with one graphical Drawing element or page.
- Enforce configurable input bytes, XML complexity, parse and extraction time, graph size, artifact size, and preparation limits before or during source preparation.
- Keep source IDs in evidence and tool contracts to preserve a future path to multi-source projects.
- Treat pairwise comparison, multi-source projects, bulk checking, uploaded packs, policy ingestion, and rule authoring as separate future workflows.

## Testing Decisions

- Test externally visible behavior rather than private helper structure.
- Prefer browser-level tests for complete user workflows and backend integration tests for deterministic contracts.
- Reuse the existing Playwright review-workflow harness for upload, chat, confirmation, Run, evidence expansion, and graph interaction.
- Add browser tests for streamed model text, tool progress, conversational follow-ups, review pause/resume, cancellation, reconnect, and claim-level evidence chips.
- Add browser tests proving an evidence chip opens the topology panel, highlights the witness, and displays explicit or inferred metadata.
- Add browser tests for direction review choices and rerunning the original operation after review.
- Add backend API tests for conversation, turn, item, event, interruption, pause, resume, and idempotency contracts.
- Add integration tests for native tool-call handling through provider adapters rather than parsing model text.
- Add provider tests proving non-tool-capable model combinations are excluded and runtime capability rejection is normalized.
- Add topology-operation tests over accepted DEXPI fixtures for complete structural witnesses, direction status, multi-candidate retrieval, boundaries, branches, and cycles.
- Add annotation tests proving exact-witness reuse and invalidation on changed source, path, or boundary.
- Add rule tests covering satisfied, violated, and indeterminate outcomes for the same rule family.
- Add negative-rule tests proving absence-based violation requires scope-completeness evidence.
- Add claim-aware truncation tests for existential matches, universal counterexamples, incomplete universal coverage, incomplete absence coverage, and explanatory partial results.
- Add Datalog proposal tests proving the capability pauses for validation and confirmation rather than executing directly.
- Extend existing generated-Datalog safety tests for predicate vocabulary, output contract, syntax, append-only behavior, filesystem restrictions, timeout, and row limits.
- Add answer-synthesis tests proving only known evidence references are accepted and unknown evidence kinds degrade to generic presentation.
- Add conversational tests proving prior prose is not accepted as evidence while valid prior evidence IDs remain usable.
- Add compaction tests proving user decisions, evidence IDs, annotations, confirmations, and limitations survive.
- Add source-preparation tests for upload bytes, XML complexity, parse timeout, graph size, artifact size, and preparation timeout diagnostics.
- Keep the existing full-page DEXPI acceptance corpus as the primary realistic regression surface.
- Add synthetic boundary fixtures only where the accepted corpus cannot produce a required limit, ambiguity, branch, cycle, or indeterminate state.
- Keep model-behavior evals for unsupported source-specific calculations, invented plant facts, ambiguity, evidence use, and limitation disclosure as regression signals rather than product certification.
- Validate documentation terminology against the witness-grounded QA contract and accepted ADRs.

## Out of Scope

- A second materialized engineering or process graph.
- Treating graphical Drawing count as a reliable P&ID page or workload boundary.
- More than one uploaded DEXPI source per OSS v1 chat.
- Pairwise P&ID comparison in the initial workflow.
- Multi-source review projects and cross-source entity alignment.
- Bulk rule-pack execution across a source collection.
- User-uploaded executable rule packs.
- Policy or standards document ingestion.
- Automatic policy-to-rule synthesis.
- Generated-query promotion into reusable rules.
- Durable personal or organizational rule approval.
- Named-standard, EPA, legal, or regulatory certification claims for demo rules.
- Automatic graph mutation, P&ID editing, or correction.
- Hydraulic simulation or source-specific calculations without required data and tools.
- Text-only model fallback through pseudo-tool parsing.
- Model quality certification, ranking, scoring, or guaranteed correctness.
- A deterministic application-owned intent compiler or topic classifier.
- Mandatory structured candidate-selection controls for conversational ambiguity.
- Full fact-database disclosure to the model by default.
- Arbitrary shell, filesystem, graph mutation, or unrestricted network tools.
- A multi-agent reviewer hierarchy in OSS v1.
- Direct dependency on OpenCode or Codex agent runtimes.
- A layout-faithful reconstruction of the source P&ID drawing.

## Further Notes

The governing principle is to control what the application can control: source validation, tool permissions, execution, provenance, evidence, limits, confirmation, and presentation of uncertainty. Model interpretation and prose remain inherently probabilistic. The application must not hide model failures, but it also must not attempt to replace model intelligence with brittle deterministic routing.

The core grounding invariant is: a process-facing relationship without its complete structural path witness is not grounded.

The core rule invariant is: no violation found is not proof of satisfaction.

The core truncation invariant is: report all grounded evidence obtained, but never turn partial coverage into a universal or absence conclusion.

The web-native harness borrows lifecycle concepts from Codex App Server and permission concepts from OpenCode, while remaining a provider-neutral, domain-specific Python implementation.

Mike OSS and Harvey demonstrate that project-scoped multi-document chat can be effective, but P&ID comparison additionally requires separate graph namespaces, source-qualified evidence, and entity alignment. Future multi-source projects should contain independent source sessions rather than one merged graph.

title: Build shared topology interpretation layer over canonical facts
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22

## What to build

Build a shared topology interpretation layer over canonical base facts / pyDEXPI full-graph facts so read-only QA tools, Datalog result witness resolution, topology evidence highlights, and rule evaluation stop reimplementing traversal semantics independently.

The layer must compute process-facing relationships as deterministic conclusions over the source graph, not as a second materialized engineering graph. Every source-specific relationship returned by the layer must include a complete ordered structural path witness with raw canonical node and edge identities plus stable topology/evidence IDs suitable for existing UI highlighting.

This work is specifically intended for model-facing tools used by an LLM: tool outputs must be compact, explicit, deterministic, validated, and safe to cite. The model may plan retrieval and prose, but backend-owned interpretation controls traversal semantics, direction evidence status, witnesses, coverage, and limitations.

## Implementation notes

Start with the direct reachable-topology behavior currently implemented in pydexpi_datalog/qa/topology_tools.py and move the semantic ownership into pydexpi_datalog/semantics. Keep topology_view and pid_view as presentation adapters. Do not introduce or persist a second engineering graph.

Use contract-first TDD. First add behavior tests over a minimal graph-facts fixture that prove complete ordered structural witnesses, raw edge identity preservation, stable topology ID resolution, and direction evidence status. Then adapt TopologyTools to delegate to the shared layer while preserving current /qa-turns behavior.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace the React graph panel.
- Do not normalize all rule outcomes in this bead.
- Do not implement generated-Datalog proposal execution in this bead.
- Do not add streaming conversation lifecycle in this bead.
- Do not persist a second graph representation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A shared topology interpretation module under pydexpi_datalog/semantics computes read-only process-facing reachability from canonical base facts / pyDEXPI full-graph facts rather than from topology_view.edges.
- [ ] Returned process-facing relationships include complete ordered structural path witnesses with raw node IDs, raw edge identities, stable topology node IDs, and stable topology edge IDs.
- [ ] Witness topology IDs are resolvable through the existing topology evidence_map used by evidence highlighting.
- [ ] Direction evidence status is computed from the witness path as explicit, inferred, or unknown, without relying on model-only inference.
- [ ] TopologyTools delegates reachable-object retrieval to the shared interpretation layer while preserving current model-facing tool behavior and /qa-turns response shape.
- [ ] Existing direct grounded QA, evidence highlight, ambiguous follow-up, and direction-review behavior remains covered by tests.
- [ ] topology_view and pid_view remain presentation adapters; the implementation does not introduce or persist a second engineering graph.
- [ ] Tests include a minimal graph-facts fixture for ordered structural witnesses and at least one E06 fixture integration path.

title: Enforce evidence sufficiency and claim validity for grounded QA answers
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22

## What to build

Add a backend-owned sufficiency gate between model tool planning and final answer acceptance. The manifest currently verifies whether a requested tool is allowed, but it does not verify whether the model used evidence that is sufficient for the user's claim. Introduce a small ReviewIntent/evidence-need contract for grounded QA turns so the backend can distinguish object lookup, structural topology relationship, rule evaluation, source mutation, conversational, and unsupported requests.

Before accepting a final answer, validate that the observed tool trace produced evidence of the required kind. A structural relationship answer must have a structural path witness, not only candidate object matches. A universal, absence, rule, or standards claim must require rule-result evidence or confirmation-required Datalog escalation; bounded local path samples must not be accepted as proof of a universal claim. Rejected/insufficient traces should return recoverable guidance to the model so it can call the correct capability or disclose that the answer is not grounded.

This bead is the sufficiency and claim-validity layer above the capability manifest. It should not add streaming, reconnect, frontend rendering, or full temporary Datalog execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Grounded QA has a typed ReviewIntent or equivalent evidence-need classification for object lookup, topology relationship, rule evaluation, source mutation, conversation, and unsupported requests.
- [ ] Final-answer acceptance validates tool trace sufficiency against the evidence need before returning an answer.
- [ ] A topology relationship answer without a structural path witness is rejected or routed back for retrieval instead of accepted from candidate matches alone.
- [ ] A universal, absence, or rule-shaped claim is rejected or escalated to confirmation-required generated logic unless rule-result evidence is present.
- [ ] Source-mutation requests are denied through the same intent/evidence path rather than treated as ordinary conversation.
- [ ] Tests cover insufficient lookup-only traces, insufficient universal claims from sampled paths, valid structural witness answers, valid conversational answers without evidence, and recoverable guidance to the model.
- [ ] Existing grounded QA, capability manifest, and direct topology QA tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement temporary Datalog execution in this bead.
- Do not add frontend streaming or reconnect behavior.
- Do not build a general-purpose frame-semantic parser. Frame-like information may inform ReviewIntent, but tool routing must be based on evidence need and backend capability policy.
close_reason: Implemented grounded QA intent/evidence sufficiency gate; python test suite passes.

title: Expose constrained witness-bearing topology operations
description: Provide validated read-only operations for tag and candidate resolution, attributes, structural neighbors, upstream and downstream traversal, constrained paths, node search, and bounded single- or multi-candidate retrieval over the pyDEXPI full graph. Every process-facing conclusion includes its structural path witness. Operations return candidate evidence without forcing application-owned ambiguity decisions.

title: Add Ollama native-tool QA provider for local model grounded chat
description:

title: Migrate web chat runtime to turn lifecycle and add Playwright coverage
description:
## What to build

Migrate the web chat runtime from the synchronous `/api/chat` path to the server-owned turn lifecycle delivered in `37x.22.24`, and add the Playwright coverage for refresh, reconnect, resume, duplicate-request, and cancellation.

The backend turn lifecycle is complete (`37x.22.24`): `POST /turns`, `GET /turns/{id}`, `GET /turns/{id}/events?after=`, `POST /turns/{id}/cancel`, `POST /turns/{id}/direction-review`, `POST /turns/{id}/datalog-review`, with disk-backed replay, typed events, request_id dedupe, and terminal cancellation. This bead consumes that surface from the frontend.

## Target

- `frontend/components/chat/pid-runtime-provider.tsx` — model adapter `run()` currently posts to `/api/chat` with `abortSignal`; rewire to the turn API.
- `frontend/lib/review-backend.ts` — backend client seam; add turn-lifecycle client calls (`POST /turns`, poll/replay `/turns/{id}/events`, resume, cancel) alongside the existing review helpers.
- `frontend/components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx` — confirmation/answer card parsers; ensure typed events map onto existing card rendering.
- `frontend/e2e/review-workflow.spec.ts` (or a new `turn-lifecycle.spec.ts`) — add the missing e2e specs.

## Change

1. Client turn transport in `review-backend.ts`: `POST /turns` to start; poll/stream `GET /turns/{id}/events?after=<seq>` and reduce typed events (`text`, `tool-progress`, `evidence`, `review-required`, `completion`, `failure`, `cancellation`) into runtime messages; cancel via `POST /turns/{id}/cancel`.
2. Rewire `pid-runtime-provider.tsx` `run()` to drive that transport; map `abortSignal` to turn cancel; on mount/reconnect, replay events from persisted turn state (survives refresh).
3. Preserve idempotency: pass a stable request_id so repeated resume/execute requests dedupe against the backend.
4. Keep direction-review and datalog-review confirmation pauses working through the turn endpoints (`/turns/{id}/direction-review`, `/turns/{id}/datalog-review`).
5. Add Playwright specs: refresh mid-turn resumes, reconnect replays events, resume is idempotent, duplicate request does not double-execute, cancellation reaches terminal state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The web client receives typed text, tool-progress, evidence, review-required, completion, failure, and cancellation events (not the synchronous `/api/chat` path).
- [ ] A paused or active turn survives refresh and reconnect and resumes from persisted state in the browser.
- [ ] Resume and tool execution are idempotent under repeated client requests.
- [ ] The user can cancel an active turn from the UI and observe a terminal cancellation state.
- [ ] Playwright refresh, reconnect, resume, duplicate-request, and cancellation tests pass; existing `.21`/`.22` e2e specs stay green.

## Notes

Split out of `37x.22.24` (backend lifecycle closed there). This is the load-bearing chat runtime every other `.22` flow depends on, so treat it as a distinct riskier surface. Precedent: `.21.6` -> `.22.4` rebaseline splits. Frontend commands (run in `frontend/`): `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:e2e`. Playwright needs a `.venv` symlink at the worktree root and `CI=1`.
close_reason: Frontend chat runtime migrated to the server-owned turn lifecycle (POST /turns, GET events, resume, cancel) with refresh/reconnect recovery. Playwright covers all 5 criteria: typed events, refresh-survives-resume, duplicate-request idempotency, active-turn cancellation, and existing .21/.22 specs stay green. E2e made hermetic via PYDEXPI_QA_PROVIDER=scripted (zero LLM/API budget). Backend 175, frontend 38 unit + 10 Playwright green. Commit d5e9654.

title: Enrich Datalog review card with interpretation, scope, assumptions, and effect
description:
## What to build

Replace the minimal 'Here is some Datalog. Run / Cancel' review card with a structured approval surface that makes engineer consent meaningful rather than ceremonial.

## Target

- `frontend/components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx` — datalog confirmation card renderer
- `pydexpi_datalog/qa/topology_tools.py` — `_propose_temporary_datalog` — add scope and assumptions fields to proposal payload
- `pydexpi_datalog/web/chainlit_review_flow.py` — pass new fields through to the frontend confirmation payload

## Change

The proposal payload should include:
- `interpretation` — plain-English restatement of what the query finds (already exists as `formal_restatement`; surface it prominently)
- `scope` — starting object, graph, direction, direction basis, path treatment
- `assumptions` — which edge types are included/excluded (process-flow, instrument, composition, recycle)
- `effect` — hardcoded: 'Read-only analysis. Does not modify the P&ID, graph, annotations, or rule pack.'
- `exact_datalog` — already present; display with syntax highlighting

The review card should offer: Approve and run / Revise interpretation / Revise query / Cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review card shows interpretation, scope, assumptions, exact Datalog, and effect before asking for approval.
- [ ] Effect line is always 'Read-only analysis. Does not modify the P&ID, graph, annotations, or rule pack.' — hardcoded, not model-generated.
- [ ] Revise interpretation and Revise query actions are available alongside Approve and Cancel.
- [ ] Existing Playwright confirmation card tests still pass.
close_reason: Proposal payload now includes interpretation, scope (starting_object_ids, graph, direction, direction_basis, path_treatment), assumptions (included/excluded edge types, recycle handling), exact_datalog, and hardcoded read-only effect. Flow passes all fields through datalog_confirmation with allowed_actions run/revise_interpretation/revise_query/cancel. Review card renders every section plus the frontend-hardcoded effect line and offers Approve and run / Revise interpretation / Revise query / Cancel. Playwright confirmation card spec extended and 10/10 green; backend and frontend suites green.

title: Persist Datalog approval audit record at execution time
description:
## What to build

Record a durable approval artifact each time a temporary Datalog proposal is approved and executed, so there is a replayable audit trail of what ran, against which graph, and when.

## Target

- `pydexpi_datalog/web/chainlit_review_flow.py` — `submit_temporary_datalog_review`
- `pydexpi_datalog/qa/topology_tools.py` — `execute_confirmed_temporary_datalog`
- New file: `pydexpi_datalog/qa/datalog_audit.py` (or alongside `topology_tools.py`)

## Change

After successful execution, persist an approval record containing:

```json
{
  "proposal_id": "<sha256-prefix>",
  "session_id": "...",
  "question": "...",
  "formal_restatement": "...",
  "generated_datalog": "...",
  "decision": "approved",
  "decided_at": "<ISO-8601>",
  "executed": true,
  "execution_status": "answered" | "execution_failed"
}
```

Write to a per-session JSONL file (e.g. `.tmp/review-sessions/{session_id}/datalog_audit.jsonl`) so records survive process restart and are independently readable.

Cancel decisions should also be recorded (`decision: canceled, executed: false`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every confirm-and-run decision appends a record to the session audit log before returning the result.
- [ ] Every cancel decision appends a record with `executed: false`.
- [ ] The audit record includes `proposal_id`, `session_id`, `question`, `formal_restatement`, `generated_datalog`, `decision`, `decided_at`, `executed`, `execution_status`.
- [ ] A unit test reads the audit log after a confirm and a cancel and asserts the expected fields.
close_reason: Confirm and cancel decisions append JSONL audit records to {artifact_root}/{session_id}/datalog_audit.jsonl via pydexpi_datalog/qa/datalog_audit.py, wired into submit_temporary_datalog_review before each return (commit 7f05ae0). Hardened by f8a249c: approvals now execute only server-stored proposals, and audit records for unknown/forged proposals record executed=false. Unit test reads the log after confirm and cancel and asserts all required fields. Backend 177/177 green.

title: PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog
description:
## Problem Statement

The repository's logic-programming story is built but not wired in. The pyDEXPI full graph is
exported into a real Souffle EDB, and a real generic-graph IDB schema
(`graph_topology_semantics.dl`) declares reusable traversal predicates — but nothing actually
executes them. Rule-pack evaluation (the `pump_discharge_check_valve` demo rule) is hand-written
Python graph traversal explicitly labeled `python_traversal`, not a logic program, despite being
presented to users as a "rule pack." The QA chat's `propose_temporary_datalog` capability — the
model's only escape hatch when read-only retrieval tools are insufficient — is a two-shape regex
shim that silently returns zero evidence for any generated Datalog beyond two exact recognized
shapes, with no error, which is worse than a rejection because it looks like "no matching
objects" instead of "this feature doesn't run your query." And even when the model does select
`propose_temporary_datalog`, there is no mid-turn mechanism connecting it to the
`generated-Datalog confirmation gate` that the frontend already renders elsewhere in the product
— the tool call is treated as satisfying the model's intent and the turn completes, meaning the
capability is a dead end in live usage today.

Process engineers cannot yet get a HAZOP-style answer (e.g. "do all pumps have isolation valves,
a check valve, and a strainer?") that is actually backed by deterministic logic execution, because
no real Souffle program runs for either the trusted rule-pack path or the model-drafted ad-hoc
path. The product's core differentiating bet — LLM drafts, deterministic logic engine verifies —
is not yet true anywhere except a narrow, single-purpose source-resolution lookup in
`source_selection.py`.

## Solution

Wire one real Souffle execution engine to serve both existing trust tiers, without merging them:

- **Bundled rule-pack trust** (repository-reviewed, e.g. `pump_discharge_check_valve`) keeps
  running immediately with no confirmation gate, but its `executable_logic` becomes a real
  Souffle program over the shared EDB/IDB schema instead of Python traversal.
- **Model-drafted ad-hoc Datalog** (`propose_temporary_datalog`) stays behind the mandatory
  `generated-Datalog confirmation gate` regardless of whether the drafted query is read-only —
  the trust axis here is reviewed-vs-unreviewed authorship, not read/write. This capability is
  wired into the `TurnLifecycleStore` pause/resume mechanism that already exists (built for a
  different, non-conversational Datalog review flow) and already has a working confirmation-card
  UI in the assistant thread — this session reuses that infrastructure rather than building new
  HITL plumbing.

To make ad-hoc queries actually useful once they execute for real, the `predicate contract`
handed to the model expands from the current two-name allowlist (`answer`, `reachable`) to the
real generic `graph_topology_semantics.dl` layer, derived dynamically per session together with
the IDB predicates of whichever rule pack(s) are loaded — read-only for ad-hoc queries, since
rule packs remain the only path that can encode new curated logic.

A typed numeric-attribute predicate is added to the schema so rules and ad-hoc queries can
compare source-provided numeric values (e.g. a pressure rating already present in the DEXPI
source) against thresholds — this does not extend to calculations requiring external formulas or
physical constants not present in the source, which must surface as `source_data_unavailable`
rather than being computed inside a rule.

Finally, a universal claim over multiple objects (e.g. "do all pumps have X, Y, and Z") can
surface more than one pending `direction review` in a single evaluation — one per object whose
flow direction is inferred rather than explicit. The existing pause/resume schema only carries a
single review item per pause; it is extended to carry a list, and the confirmation UI renders all
pending items in one batched card instead of pausing once per item.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want a repository-bundled rule (like pump discharge check valve) to
   actually execute as a real logic program against the loaded source, so that "rule pack" means
   what it says instead of hidden Python traversal.
2. As a process engineer, I want the same rule-evaluation contract (satisfied/violated/
   indeterminate, evidence, scope-completeness) to hold whether the rule runs as Python or
   Souffle, so that existing evidence presentation and testing keep working unchanged.
3. As a process engineer, I want to ask a formal or recursive question in the chat and have the
   model's drafted Datalog actually execute once I approve it, so that `propose_temporary_datalog`
   is a real capability instead of a dead end.
4. As a process engineer, I want every model-drafted query to require my explicit confirmation
   before it runs, regardless of whether it's read-only, so that generated logic never executes
   silently and I retain the same trust guarantee the product has always promised.
5. As a process engineer, I want the confirmation card for a drafted query to show plain-language
   meaning and scope first, with the generated Datalog collapsed but inspectable, so that I can
   approve intended semantics without reading code first.
6. As a process engineer, I want to see a clear, specific error when a drafted query is invalid
   or unsafe, so that "no evidence found" never silently means "this feature is broken."
7. As a process engineer, I want a drafted query to be able to reference the same predicate
   vocabulary a bundled rule pack uses (read-only), so that ad-hoc questions can build on existing
   curated logic instead of starting from a two-predicate allowlist.
8. As a process engineer, I want a drafted query to be validated against a real, complete
   predicate contract rather than a hardcoded two-name allowlist, so that recursion, joins, and
   real constraints actually work instead of silently returning nothing.
9. As a process engineer, I want to compare an actual numeric value already present in the source
   (e.g. a pressure rating) against a threshold in a rule or drafted query, so that HAZOP-style
   quantitative checks are possible without inventing data.
10. As a process engineer, I want a rule or query that needs data or formulas not present in the
    source to say so explicitly, so that missing engineering inputs are never silently assumed or
    invented.
11. As a process engineer, I want to ask a universal question about many objects at once (e.g.
    "do all pumps have an isolation valve, a check valve, and a strainer") and get one evaluation
    covering every resolved object, so that I don't have to ask the same question N times.
12. As a process engineer, I want every object in a universal evaluation with an ambiguous
    (inferred) flow direction to be raised for my review together in one place, so that I'm not
    interrupted repeatedly for the same evaluation.
13. As a process engineer, I want to confirm, reverse, or mark unknown each pending direction
    review independently within that one batched card, so that resolving one doesn't force a
    particular answer on the others.
14. As a process engineer, I want an object whose direction I mark unknown to remain
    indeterminate for that claim rather than being silently excluded or guessed, so that
    uncertainty stays visible in the final answer.
15. As a process engineer, I want the final answer to a universal claim to report satisfied,
    violated, and indeterminate objects individually with their own evidence, so that "mostly
    fine" isn't flattened into a false yes or no.
16. As a process engineer, I want a universal claim to be explicitly disclosed as incomplete when
    my object enumeration itself was truncated, so that partial coverage never quietly reads as a
    complete answer.
17. As a process engineer, I want an off-topic question (e.g. "what model am I talking to") to get
    a brief, honest acknowledgment before being redirected back to P&ID review, so that the
    assistant doesn't feel like it's refusing to talk to me.
18. As a process engineer, I want a follow-up question that refers back to something established
    earlier in the conversation to be answered by reusing that evidence, without the assistant
    needing to redo the same Datalog work, so that conversations stay efficient.
19. As a process engineer, I want any evidence identity cited in an answer — whether newly
    retrieved or reused from earlier in the conversation — to be checked against the current
    topology, so that stale or hallucinated references never pass as evidence.
20. As a developer, I want rule-pack evaluation and ad-hoc query execution to share one real
    Souffle execution path, so that there is exactly one place that runs Datalog and one place to
    harden its safety, timeout, and validation behavior.
21. As a developer, I want the predicate contract exposed to the model to be derived
    programmatically from the EDB/IDB schema and loaded rule-pack declarations, so that it never
    drifts out of sync with the actual schema by hand.
22. As a developer, I want the existing `test_bundled_rule_pack.py` contract tests to continue
    passing unmodified against the Souffle-backed evaluator, so that the migration has a built-in
    regression net instead of needing a parallel test rewrite.
23. As a developer, I want the `TurnLifecycleStore` pause/resume mechanism, already proven for a
    different Datalog-review flow, reused for the QA chat's confirmation gate rather than a new
    mechanism invented, so that pause/resume/cancel semantics stay consistent across the product.
24. As a developer, I want the review-required event payload to support a list of pending items,
    not just one, so that batched direction review has a place to live without a second schema.

## Implementation Decisions

- One real `souffle` execution path serves both repository-bundled rule-pack evaluation and
  model-drafted ad-hoc Datalog (`propose_temporary_datalog`), replacing the current Python
  traversal implementation (`bundled_rule_pack.py`) and the two-shape regex shim
  (`topology_tools.py`'s temporary-Datalog executor) respectively. These remain two separate
  trust tiers on the same engine, not one merged permission model.
- Bundled rule packs keep executing immediately, without a confirmation step, against the full
  EDB/IDB schema (`graph_facts_schema.dl` + `graph_topology_semantics.dl` + rule-pack-specific
  predicates).
- Model-drafted ad-hoc Datalog keeps the mandatory `generated-Datalog confirmation gate`
  regardless of whether the drafted query is read-only. There is no read-only exception — this
  was considered and rejected because the product's actual trust axis is reviewed-vs-unreviewed
  authorship, not read/write.
- `grounded_qa_harness`'s rule-evaluation intent path is wired so that a `propose_temporary_datalog`
  call raises the same `needs_datalog_confirmation` status the `TurnLifecycleStore` already
  supports, pausing the turn instead of treating a `confirmation_required` tool result as
  satisfying the intent and completing the turn.
- The existing confirmation-card UI (assistant thread, Run/Revise/Cancel) is reused for the QA
  chat's confirmation flow rather than building a new HITL surface; this is an integration of
  existing infrastructure into a code path that never used it, not new UI.
- The predicate contract given to the model for `propose_temporary_datalog` is derived
  dynamically per session: the generic `graph_topology_semantics.dl` predicate set, plus the IDB
  predicates declared by whichever rule pack(s) are loaded in that session, exposed read-only.
  Rule-pack predicates are not exposed as a mutable or extensible surface to ad-hoc queries —
  only as join targets.
- A typed numeric-attribute predicate (derived from the existing symbol-typed `node_attribute`
  via Souffle's `to_number()`) is added to the schema so both rule packs and ad-hoc queries can
  perform arithmetic comparisons against source-provided numeric values. Calculations requiring
  external formulas, correlations, or physical constants not present in the source graph remain
  explicitly out of scope and must be reported via the existing `source_data_unavailable`
  grounding posture, never computed inline.
- Object classification for rule logic (e.g. "is this a check valve") uses the existing
  `node_label` predicate, which is already fed from the same source attribute other parts of the
  codebase use as `class_name` — no new fact-export work is required to support type-based
  predicates.
- Universal/absence-style claims over multiple resolved objects (e.g. a "do all pumps have X"
  question) are evaluated as one Datalog program over all resolved identities, not one query per
  object, so the confirmation step itself stays singular even when the claim spans many objects.
- The `TurnLifecycleStore` review-required payload is extended from a single review object to a
  list of pending review items, to support a `direction review` surfacing more than one ambiguous
  object from the same evaluation. The confirmation UI renders all pending items in one card, each
  independently resolvable (confirm/reverse/mark unknown), rather than pausing once per item.
  Marking an item's direction unknown leaves that specific object's outcome `indeterminate` for
  the claim, permanently for that evaluation (not re-askable within it).
- Any evidence reference cited in a final answer — whether obtained via a tool call this turn or
  reused from an earlier turn's `grounded_evidence_ids` — continues to be validated against
  current `known_evidence_ids` before being accepted as grounding; this existing invariant is
  unchanged and is the correct enforcement point for follow-up questions, not a new deterministic
  follow-up classifier.
- The `out_of_scope` grounding-posture policy text is extended to explicitly permit a brief,
  honest acknowledgment of a general/off-topic question before redirecting back to P&ID review,
  instead of implying a bare non-answer. This remains model-owned behavior, not a backend
  classifier, consistent with the existing decision not to build a deterministic intent compiler.
- A prior session handoff's claim that rule-pack verification already runs real recursive Datalog
  is incorrect and is not prior art; see ADR 0008 for the corrected record.

## Testing Decisions

- Test the two existing public seams, not new ones: `run_grounded_qa_turn(...)` in
  `grounded_qa_harness.py` (confirmation-gate wiring, ad-hoc Souffle execution, dynamic predicate
  contract, batched direction review, pause/resume via `TurnLifecycleStore`), and
  `evaluate_bundled_rule(...)` in `bundled_rule_pack.py` (rule-pack Souffle execution, numeric
  attribute comparisons). Prefer these over a new shared seam, since each already has an
  established test suite.
- `tests/verification/test_bundled_rule_pack.py` is prior art and its existing assertions (outcome,
  evidence shape, scope-completeness, direction-review gating) are the regression net for the
  Souffle rewrite — they assert on the public contract, not Python-traversal internals, and should
  continue to pass unmodified.
- `tests/qa/test_grounded_qa_harness.py` and `tests/web/test_turn_lifecycle.py` are prior art for
  pause/resume, confirmation, and round-progress behavior; extend rather than replace.
- Add tests proving `propose_temporary_datalog` confirmation actually pauses the turn
  (`needs_datalog_confirmation`) and that `Run` resumes into real Souffle execution with real
  results, not the two-shape shim's silent-empty behavior.
- Add tests proving invalid or unsafe drafted Datalog produces an explicit validation error, not a
  silent empty result.
- Add tests proving the predicate contract handed to the model reflects the loaded rule pack(s)'
  IDB predicates in addition to the generic schema.
- Add tests proving a numeric-attribute comparison rule correctly classifies satisfied/violated/
  indeterminate outcomes using real source values.
- Add a test proving a universal claim over multiple resolved objects with multiple ambiguous
  directions produces one batched review-required pause listing all pending items, and that each
  item is independently resolvable.
- Add a test proving a follow-up question's cited evidence reference (reused from a prior turn) is
  still validated against current `known_evidence_ids` and rejected if stale/hallucinated.
- Add a test/eval-harness case for the `out_of_scope` acknowledgment-before-redirect behavior,
  as a regression prompt rather than a deterministic assertion on exact wording.
- Avoid asserting on private Souffle subprocess invocation details; assert on the public
  evaluation/execution result contract, matching existing prior art.
- All of the above use scripted fake providers (matching existing prior art like
  `ScriptedQATurnProvider` and the custom fake providers in `test_grounded_qa_harness.py`), not a
  real model — they prove the harness correctly executes, gates, and validates a given tool call,
  not that a real model will choose to draft a correct one.
- Add a minimal live-model verification pass, in the same style used to verify the round-limit fix
  this session (real OpenRouter/BYOK model, live before/after comparison, not just green scripted
  tests): a small, fixed set of real natural-language questions — including at least one
  HAZOP-style universal claim (e.g. "do all pumps have an isolation valve, a check valve, and a
  strainer") and one numeric-threshold question — run against a real tool-calling model, checked
  for a correctly drafted Datalog query, correct confirmation-gate behavior, and a correct final
  outcome. This is not the full graded regression suite against `TrainingTestCases/` (that remains
  separate, out-of-scope future work) — it is a small, manual/scripted proof that the wiring
  produces a correct real answer at least once per capability, not just a proof that scripted
  inputs are handled correctly.

## Out of Scope

- A graded regression eval harness against `TrainingTestCases/` claiming measurable accuracy
  improvement over other tools — tracked separately.
- Replacing the keyword-based intent classifier (`_classify_review_intent`) for initial
  lookup-vs-rule-evaluation routing — remains a pre-retrieval heuristic by design; only
  object-reference disambiguation (via `find_equipment` result counts) is in scope, not intent
  routing.
- Any read-only exception to the `generated-Datalog confirmation gate` — rejected as inconsistent
  with the product's reviewed-vs-unreviewed trust axis.
- Migrating `find_equipment` / `get_reachable_equipment` to Souffle-backed query templates — these
  remain fast, trusted Python/NetworkX lookups; only rule-pack evaluation and ad-hoc generated
  Datalog move to real Souffle execution.
- Supporting calculations that require external formulas, correlations, or physical constants not
  present in the DEXPI source — these must be reported as `source_data_unavailable`, not computed.
- Promoting a user-confirmed ad-hoc query into a reusable rule-pack rule — confirmation remains
  temporary execution consent only, per the existing `Datalog proposal capability` design.
- Rewriting the pause/resume mechanism itself — it already exists and works; this PRD only
  extends its payload shape to support a list of review items and connects the QA chat's
  confirmation-required path into it for the first time.

## Further Notes

This PRD corrects a real misconception surfaced during scoping: the repository's real Souffle
execution today is limited to a single narrow subprocess call in `source_selection.py` for source
resolution. Both the demo rule pack and the QA chat's ad-hoc Datalog capability are currently
non-Datalog stand-ins (Python traversal and a regex shim, respectively), despite being presented
to users as logic-programming capabilities. See `docs/adr/0008-one-souffle-engine-for-rule-packs-and-ad-hoc-queries.md`
for the full architectural decision record, including rejected alternatives.

This work is the direct realization of the product's original bet (LLM drafts, deterministic
Datalog engine verifies) for both the trusted rule-pack path and the conversational ad-hoc path,
and should be treated as foundational rather than incremental — most of the QA chat's
grounding/evidence/confirmation guarantees are currently unproven in practice because nothing
downstream of `propose_temporary_datalog` actually executes.

title: QA chat confirmation gate wiring, Claude-Code-style inline widget
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Wire the QA chat's `propose_temporary_datalog` capability into the existing
`TurnLifecycleStore` pause/resume mechanism (`needs_datalog_confirmation` status), which today
exists but is never entered from this code path — a `confirmation_required` tool result is
currently treated as satisfying the model's intent, and the turn completes without the query ever
running. This capability is a dead end in live usage until this is fixed.

Render a new, purpose-built confirmation widget inline in the chat thread — a boxed, numbered,
keyboard-navigable choice prompt in the style of Claude Code's interactive tool-approval prompt
(arrow keys / number keys to select, Enter to confirm), not the existing button-based
Run/Revise/Cancel card built for a different, non-conversational Datalog review flow. The widget
shows the plain-language restatement and scope first, with the generated Datalog collapsed but
inspectable, consistent with the product's existing `intent-first confirmation` decision.

No trust escalation: every `propose_temporary_datalog` call requires its own confirmation. There
is no "don't ask again this session" — that was explicitly considered and rejected as
inconsistent with the confirmation gate being temporary execution consent, not reusable-rule
promotion.

This slice does not require the ad-hoc executor to be real Souffle yet (that's the next slice) —
resuming after confirmation may still invoke today's narrow two-shape executor. The point of this
slice is closing the dead end: a user can now actually get to "Run" and receive a result, even a
limited one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `propose_temporary_datalog` call results in the turn pausing with status
      `needs_datalog_confirmation`, not silently completing.
- [ ] The new boxed/numbered/keyboard-navigable widget renders inline in the chat thread showing
      plain-language restatement, scope, and collapsed generated Datalog.
- [ ] Selecting "Run" resumes the turn via `TurnLifecycleStore.resume()` and produces a final
      answer from the (still-current) executor.
- [ ] Selecting "Revise" or "Cancel" produces the same non-executing outcomes the existing
      confirmation flow defines (nothing executed, user prompted to clarify or told it was
      canceled).
- [ ] A full-stack Playwright test: a real question is typed into the running web app's chat, the
      widget appears, "Run" is selected via keyboard, and a result renders — exercising the real
      browser and a real backend turn, not just the Python harness function in isolation.
- [ ] No mechanism exists anywhere that allows a later `propose_temporary_datalog` call in the
      same session to skip confirmation.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

Frontend files (datalog-confirmation-widget.tsx, datalog-confirmation-gate.spec.ts, thread.tsx routing) remain uncommitted pending the 2ki.11/2ki.12 stepped-cards stack landing.

title: Ad-hoc Datalog executes via real Souffle
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Replace the two-shape regex shim in the ad-hoc Datalog executor (which pattern-matches exactly
`answer("literal_id").` and `answer(x) :- reachable("some_id", x).` and silently returns zero
evidence for anything else) with a genuine `souffle` subprocess execution, the same way
`source_selection.py` already shells out to `souffle` today. The predicate set stays the current
narrow `{answer, reachable}` allowlist for this slice — expanding it is the next slice. The goal
here is fixing the silent-wrong-answer bug: a query outside the recognized shapes must now either
execute for real or fail with an explicit, specific validation/execution error, never silently
return "no matching objects" when the real issue is "this feature doesn't run your query."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirmed ad-hoc queries execute via a real `souffle` subprocess call, not text pattern
      matching.
- [ ] A query using only `answer`/`reachable` in the previously-supported shapes produces the same
      results as before (no regression for the two shapes already relied on).
- [ ] An invalid or unsafe query produces an explicit, specific error, never a silent empty
      result.
- [ ] A full-stack Playwright test: a real natural-language question that requires the confirmed
      query to actually execute (not just be accepted) is typed into the running web app, the
      widget from the confirmation-gate slice is used to Run it, and the browser shows a real,

description:

real Souffle rule-pack execution path landed in the "Rule packs run on real Souffle" slice.

      `to_number()` from existing symbol-typed attribute facts, with no changes to fact export.
- [ ] At least one concrete rule using a numeric threshold comparison (e.g. a pressure-rating
      check) executes correctly via real Souffle and returns satisfied/violated/indeterminate as
      appropriate.
- [ ] A source object missing the relevant numeric attribute produces an explicit
      `source_data_unavailable`-equivalent outcome, not an invented value or false pass.

title: Expand ad-hoc predicate contract to generic schema + rule-pack IDB
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Replace the ad-hoc query executor's hardcoded two-name predicate allowlist (`{answer,
reachable}`) with a predicate contract derived programmatically from the real schema: the generic
`graph_topology_semantics.dl` predicates, plus the IDB predicates declared by whichever rule
pack(s) are loaded in the current session, exposed read-only to ad-hoc queries. Rule packs are
not made mutable or extensible through this — only usable as join targets in the model's drafted
query. This unlocks recursion, joins, and real formal constraints in `propose_temporary_datalog`
that the two-shape shim could never support, and is the payoff for the real-execution work landed
in the previous slice.

The predicate contract must be derived from the schema/declarations, not hand-maintained as a
second list that can drift out of sync.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The model-facing predicate contract for `propose_temporary_datalog` reflects the current
      generic schema predicates plus the loaded rule pack(s)' IDB predicates, computed from the
      schema/rule-pack declarations rather than hardcoded.
- [ ] A confirmed query using a predicate beyond `{answer, reachable}` (e.g. a join against
      `direct_process_connection` or a loaded rule-pack predicate) executes correctly and returns
      real results.
- [ ] A confirmed query attempting to use a predicate not in the current contract (e.g. from an
      unloaded rule pack) is rejected with an explicit validation error.
- [ ] A live-model check: a real natural-language question requiring a real join or recursive
      constraint beyond the old shim's two shapes is correctly drafted and answered by a real
      tool-capable model.

  predicate contract is only meaningful once queries actually execute for real.

Predicate contract is derived from graph facts/topology semantics declarations plus loaded rule-pack IDB declarations; confirmed ad-hoc programs execute over graph_facts + graph_topology_semantics + loaded rule-pack IDB + answer query. title: Batched direction review, same widget pattern
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34 (PRD: Real Souffle execution for rule packs and ad-hoc Datalog)

## What to build

Extend `TurnLifecycleStore`'s review-required payload from a single review object to a list of
pending review items, so that a universal claim over multiple resolved objects (e.g. "do all
pumps have an isolation valve, a check valve, and a strainer") can surface more than one
ambiguous `direction review` (one per object with inferred rather than explicit flow direction)
in a single pause, instead of only supporting one pending item at a time.

Render all pending items in one instance of the boxed/numbered/keyboard-navigable widget built
for the ad-hoc confirmation gate — each item independently resolvable (confirm / reverse / mark
unknown) within that single widget, not N sequential pauses. Marking an item's direction unknown
leaves that specific object's outcome `indeterminate` for the claim permanently within that
evaluation (not re-askable).

The final answer for the universal claim must report satisfied/violated/indeterminate per object
individually, each with its own evidence chip and structural path witness — not a single flattened
yes/no.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The review-required event payload supports a list of pending direction-review items, not
      just one.
- [ ] A universal claim producing multiple ambiguous-direction objects in one evaluation pauses
      once, with all pending items visible in one widget.
- [ ] Each pending item can be resolved (confirm/reverse/unknown) independently of the others
      within that same widget, without forcing a single answer on all of them.
- [ ] An item marked unknown remains `indeterminate` for that claim and is not re-prompted within
      the same evaluation.
- [ ] The final answer reports per-object outcomes (satisfied/violated/indeterminate) with
      individual evidence chips, not a single flattened result.
- [ ] A full-stack Playwright test: a real universal question over multiple objects with at least
      two objects needing direction review is run against the real web app, and the batched
      widget with multiple independently-resolvable items is exercised end-to-end in the browser.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-37x.22.34.6 (Expand ad-hoc predicate contract to generic schema + rule-pack
  IDB) — needs a real multi-object universal-claim query capability to produce multiple ambiguous
  directions in one evaluation.
close_reason: Landed as 002ea67. Direction-review pause payload now carries direction_reviews[] while preserving legacy direction_review; API accepts batched per-item decisions; UI renders one batched widget with numbered independently-resolvable items; unknown decisions become indeterminate per-object outcomes. Validated with focused pytest/API checks, frontend node tests, and typecheck; Playwright remains blocked by unrelated upload/filechooser stack flakiness.

title: Enable model-planned retrieval and generated-logic escalation
description: Expose constrained read-only topology and bundled-rule tools plus a confirmation-required propose_datalog_query capability to a tool-eligible model. A Datalog proposal produces generated logic and an engineer-readable restatement, then pauses for backend validation and user confirmation; it never executes directly. title: Return justified tri-state rule evaluation outcomes
description: Represent every rule evaluation as satisfied, violated, or indeterminate with evidence. Satisfaction requires proof over the defined claim and scope. Absence-based violation requires complete evaluated scope and scope-completeness evidence. Apply claim-aware truncation: retain all grounded partial evidence, allow witnessed existential matches and counterexamples where logically sufficient, and return indeterminate when truncated coverage cannot prove a universal or absence conclusion.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

title: Separate query confirmation from reusable rule-pack trust
description: Treat all model-generated Datalog plus restatement as temporary confirmed query pairs, even when generated text appears source-independent. Never infer, suggest, or persist generated logic as a reusable rule in OSS v1. Only exact versioned repository-bundled rule-pack rules are reusable and trusted. User-uploaded executable rule packs, generated-query promotion, and durable user rule storage are out of scope.

Resolved during grill-with-docs: OSS v1 supports repository-bundled executable rule packs only. User-uploaded executable packs, Markdown policy-source uploads, policy-to-rule synthesis, and generated-query promotion are disallowed. Those capabilities belong to a future paid rule-authoring tier.
