title: PRD: Reasoning-architecture benchmark - LLM-direct vs engine-mediated grounded P&ID QA
description:
## Problem Statement

The product owner is losing confidence in the engine-mediated architecture. In live use the current system disappoints: answers sound weird, turns are slow, and the LLM frequently fails to generate correct Datalog (two live incidents this week: helper-predicate rejection, missing .output line). Meanwhile frontier LLMs with CoT look good enough that the entire NL->Datalog->confirm->Souffle pipeline may be unnecessary ceremony. We have no evidence either way, and the decision is too consequential to make on vibes. Cost matters: the company wants to know whether a cheap OSS model (DeepSeek v4) can perform under whichever architecture wins.

## Solution

A benchmark that produces a pre-committed verdict. Three arms plus a direct mode, three models, ~75 questions across three slices over real and synthetic drawings, programmatically graded with witness verification. The decision rule is locked BEFORE any runs so results cannot be argued into prior beliefs:

- Verdict tier: Claude Sonnet + GPT (mid-frontier, deliberately not best-of-frontier).
- If EITHER scores <98% exact-verdict accuracy (with checkable witnesses) on the compliance/universal slice under the strongest Arm-A configuration, we build the new engine-mediated system.
- Only if BOTH pass do we stand down.
- Retrieval/local slice bar: 95% with witnesses.
- DeepSeek v4 runs everywhere as the cost story; it never decides the verdict.
- Trap-slice scores are reported, never gate. Prose quality and latency inform the follow-on spec, never overturn correctness.

Output: a results report (per arm x model x slice x graph-size bucket, with per-episode transcripts) and the locked verdict recorded on the tracker. The spec of the chosen NL<->logic loop is a follow-on effort.

## User Stories

1. As the product owner, I want a pre-committed decision rule, so that benchmark results trigger a verdict instead of a debate.
2. As the product owner, I want the challenger arm faithful to published research (DAR-style: agentic LLM + terminal + files), so the comparison tests the real alternative, not a strawman.
3. As the product owner, I want an Arm A-direct mode (single pass, entire XML in context, no tools), so my 1M-token-context intuition is tested directly.
4. As the product owner, I want DeepSeek v4 in every arm, so I learn whether a cheap OSS model becomes viable when the engine does the reasoning.
5. As the product owner, I want Arm C (agent + Souffle + rule packs, iterating against terminal output), because it embodies the CODORD generate-revise loop and is the leading candidate for the new system.
6. As the product owner, I want the incumbent pipeline (Arm B) benchmarked as-is, so any replacement is justified against what exists.
7. As a process engineer, I want every answer to carry witness object IDs I can check on the drawing, so I can trust a verdict without trusting prose.
8. As a process engineer, I want off-domain or unanswerable questions redirected gracefully (what CAN be checked), not refused with 'not a P&ID question'.
9. As the product owner, I want a trap slice (~15 unanswerable/ambiguous/off-domain questions) scored on grounded refusal and graceful redirect, so hallucination-under-pressure is measured, not anecdotal.
10. As the product owner, I want ~30 hand-authored QA pairs over the real DEXPI training fixtures with ground truth I personally sign off, so the benchmark reflects real drawings.
11. As the product owner, I want ~30 synthetic truth-by-construction questions over generated drawings with a graph-size sweep, so we measure where (or whether) LLM-direct degrades with scale instead of assuming it.
12. As a benchmark operator, I want the dataset to be data files validated by a loader (every witness ID must exist in its drawing), so bad ground truth fails fast.
13. As a benchmark operator, I want a single entry point (run manifest -> report), so running the matrix is one command.
14. As a benchmark operator, I want per-episode capture of tokens, cost, wall time, and full transcripts, so cost and fairness are auditable.
15. As the product owner, I want equal tool/round budgets across agentic arms and published transcripts, so nobody can claim the challenger was hobbled.
16. As the product owner, I want agents in Arms A/C to load the drawing into NetworkX (node-link/GraphML export shipped alongside XML and graph-facts), so the challenger is steel-manned with general-purpose computation.
17. As the product owner, I want agents to run their code, see real output, and revise before submitting -- executed results, not code suggestions -- so users receive answers, not homework.
18. As a benchmark operator, I want scripted/fake-model tests of every arm adapter and the grader, so CI never makes live LLM calls.
19. As a future implementer, I want the results report broken out per slice, model, arm, and size bucket, so the follow-on loop spec inherits evidence, not averages.
20. As the product owner, I want the verdict recorded as a tracker decision referencing the report, so the architecture choice is citable later.

## Implementation Decisions

- One new seam: a benchmark package whose public entry is run_benchmark(manifest) -> report, with a thin CLI wrapper. Everything else internal.
- Arm adapter contract: (question, drawing bundle) -> StructuredAnswer {verdict, witness IDs, posture, transcript, usage}. All arms emit it.
- Arms: A = agentic sandbox (DEXPI XML + derived graph-facts + NetworkX export + README; terminal access; NO Souffle, NO rule packs, NO confirmation machinery -- Arm A excludes only OUR bespoke machinery; general-purpose computation is explicitly allowed). A-direct = single-pass full-context prompt, no harness. B = existing app pipeline driven at its existing public boundary, unmodified (its confirmation gate stays: it is the incumbent measured as-is). C = Arm A sandbox + Souffle on PATH + bundled rule-pack markdown.
- Agent harness: Harbor/Terminus-KIRA (the DAR paper's released stack) is the PRIMARY path for Arms A and C -- the model drives a terminal in a sandboxed episode, iterates against real output, and submits through KIRA's verification gate. First implementation step is a timeboxed integration spike: our model endpoints, our task format, structured verdict+witness extraction from the episode. Only if integration fails for documented cause do we fall back to an in-house thin loop on the existing provider abstraction with a KIRA-style submission gate, with the deviation recorded in the report.
- No pre-execution human confirmation in candidate arms (product owner decision, 2026-07-09): agents execute their own read-only analysis (python/NetworkX, Souffle in C), observe real output, revise, and return executed results. The confirm-before-execute gate on generated Datalog is dropped as a requirement for the future system; consent ceremony is replaced by post-hoc auditability -- the exact executed program and witness set ship with every answer, inspectable on demand. (Safety basis: the analysis executor is strictly read-only; it cannot modify the P&ID, graph, annotations, or rule packs.)
- Dataset: manifests as data (question, slice, drawing ref, ground truth verdict + witness set). Three slices: 30 hand-authored over TrainingTestCases fixtures (SME-signed), 30 synthetic truth-by-construction with injected violations across a size sweep, ~15 trap. Synthetic drawings ship as XML plus pre-derived graph-facts for all arms; if full DEXPI-valid synthesis proves too costly, fall back to a minimal XML wrapper around graph-level truth and document the fidelity limit.
- Grading: pure function (answer, ground truth, graph facts) -> grade. Exact verdict match; witness sets verified against the graph; trap rubric grades grounded refusal + graceful redirect (LLM-judged informational, human spot-checked).
- Decision rule as stated in Solution; encoded in the report generator so the verdict line is computed, not written.
- Models: Sonnet, GPT, DeepSeek v4 through the existing provider layer.

## Testing Decisions

- Behavior tests at the package seam with scripted arms/providers, following the existing ScriptedQATurnProvider pattern (prior art: the grounded-QA harness behavioral tests and the web TestClient suites).
- Grader gets the heaviest unit coverage: verdict matching, witness verification edge cases (missing, extra, unknown IDs), trap rubric boundaries.
- Dataset loader tests: manifests with unknown witness IDs or malformed ground truth are rejected.
- No live LLM calls anywhere in the test suite; live matrix runs are executions producing report artifacts, not tests. Terminus episodes are exercised in tests via a scripted model behind the same episode interface.

## Out of Scope

- Building the new production system or the NL<->logic loop spec (follow-on effort after the verdict; that spec now specifies the audit-trail presentation -- executed program + witnesses disclosure -- rather than a confirmation gate).
- Adopting a deontic/modal reasoning framework (Ergo/Rulelog/ASP) for its own sake.
- UI/frontend work; changes to the current app beyond what driving Arm B at its existing boundary requires.

## Further Notes

- Research grounding: DAR (arXiv 2606.05009) -- agentic harnesses lift frontier models but collapse weak ones, best frontier ~0.86-0.89 on numeric statutory tasks; harness choice worth tens of points (hence adopting the paper's own harness as primary). CODORD framing: the LLM closes the NL->logic authoring gap; the engine stays for determinism, exhaustiveness, and witnesses.
- Dropping the confirmation gate reverses the premise behind the first-confirmation-trust model (Interactive rule authoring epic, 2yr) and the confirmation-gate work in the witness-grounded QA epic; those beads are NOT modified by this spec -- the post-verdict follow-on re-charts them.
- The graph-size sweep exists to measure long-context degradation on exhaustive quantification empirically -- 1M-token windows may well hold entire drawings; whether attention holds for universal checks is the open question.
- Ties into existing bead: Evaluate GraphML as topology view interchange (37x.21.12) -- the NetworkX export may satisfy it.
- Relation to the LLM-assisted-logic epic (3qo): this benchmark decides whether that epic's premise survives.

comments.text: Delivered the synthetic truth-by-construction slice (pydexpi_datalog/benchmark/synthetic.py + synthetic-slice CLI command). (1) Declared size sweep: small/medium/large = 1/3/8 pump trains with base discharge runs 1/3/6 (drawing 4 per bucket deepens runs +4); 5 drawings per bucket, 15 total, strictly increasing node counts across buckets (asserted). Violations injected per a deterministic per-bucket layout: compliant / check-valve / diameter / both-on-different-trains / deep-compliant. (2) Every drawing is a 3q1.4-layout bundle (drawing.xml, graph_facts.json, graph.json, README.md) written through a new shared export seam write_bundle_derivatives; validate_bundle passes and build_souffle_harbor_task consumes a generated bundle end-to-end (EDB rendered from synthetic facts). (3) 30 loader-valid entries; ground truth emitted directly from the construction record (violating pump IDs accumulated while building trains - no hand labeling) and cross-checked question-by-question against real Souffle 2.5 output of both demo rule-pack programs (skipif-guarded; ran green locally, rule_unresolved empty everywhere). (4) size_bucket recorded per entry and carried through the loader as BenchmarkQuestion.size_bucket for the 3q1.13 report to break out accuracy by graph size. title: PRD: Add LLM-assisted logic requests for deterministic P&ID QA
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers and EPC users need a way to ask natural-language questions about P&IDs and turn informal review rules into executable deterministic checks without hand-writing Datalog. The current system already has a trusted DEXPI 1.3 source-file to graph-facts to derived Souffle predicate pipeline, plus deterministic query artifacts, but it requires humans to know the query corpus, predicate vocabulary, and Datalog-oriented execution seams.

The user wants frontier LLM assistance without making the LLM the compliance answer source. The LLM should help refine vague requests, route non-logic questions, draft Datalog for topology QA, and explain deterministic results. The answer source must remain deterministic execution over the approved predicate contract. Small customers should eventually use app-managed credits plus overage, while the first CLI slice can use OPENAI_API_KEY.

## Solution

Add a CLI-artifact logic workflow for LLM-assisted logic requests. A logic request starts as a user-authored natural-language request and may be refined, routed, drafted into generated Datalog plus an engineer-readable formal restatement, confirmed by the user, and then executed against an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl artifact.

The first implementation should be text-only, OpenAI-backed, and orchestrated by repository-owned Python code rather than autonomous agent tool use. The LLM may draft Datalog and restatements, but Python controls routing, validation, repair attempts, confirmation boundaries, Souffle execution, artifacts, and diagnostics. The deterministic result artifact remains primary; any final LLM explanation is supplemental.

V1 should support hybrid QA request routing. Not every request should become Datalog. Documentation and metadata questions can be answered through cheaper faithful paths. Unsupported engineering requests should produce missing-capability artifacts instead of invented answers. Topology QA logic requests should use only the approved predicate contract by default, with generic raw attributes gated behind an explicit advanced raw-attribute mode.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want to enter a natural-language P&ID question, so that I do not need to write Datalog by hand.
2. As a process engineer, I want vague requests to be refined before logic generation, so that the system does not guess hidden assumptions.
3. As a process engineer, I want the system to classify whether my request needs Datalog, metadata lookup, documentation, clarification, or is unsupported, so that not every question is forced into logic.
4. As a process engineer, I want the LLM to draft Datalog from a topology QA logic request, so that natural language can become executable deterministic logic.
5. As a process engineer, I want to review a formal restatement of the generated logic, so that I can confirm intent without reading Datalog.
6. As a process engineer, I want the formal restatement to include if-then conditions, negation, logical operators, exceptions, and scope, so that the rule semantics are inspectable.
7. As a process engineer, I want the system to execute generated Datalog only after I confirm the paired Datalog and restatement, so that logic does not run against my plant unexpectedly.
8. As a process engineer, I want deterministic query results to be shown before any LLM explanation, so that I can distinguish facts from prose.
9. As a process engineer, I want the LLM to explain deterministic results in plain language, so that I can understand the output without losing traceability.
10. As a process engineer, I want unsupported requests to return missing facts, missing predicates, missing policy, or external-tool requirements, so that I know what capability is absent.
11. As a process engineer, I want topology questions to run over approved graph and topology predicates, so that answers are grounded in the derived semantics layer.
12. As a process engineer, I want generic raw attribute querying to be opt-in, so that normal queries do not depend accidentally on messy source attribute names.
13. As a process engineer, I want the command to work against an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl file, so that I can use the artifact seam the repo already trusts.
14. As a process engineer, I want syntax and safety diagnostics before confirmation, so that I do not review invalid logic.
15. As a process engineer, I want generated Datalog repair attempts to be bounded, so that the system does not loop indefinitely or burn cost.
16. As a process engineer, I want documentation questions to be answered from project docs or predicate documentation, so that simple conceptual questions do not require Datalog execution.
17. As a process engineer, I want metadata questions to be answered from artifacts, so that I can inspect runs without invoking unnecessary logic generation.
18. As a process engineer, I want final artifacts to record which model and context policy were used, so that I can assess trust and reproducibility.
19. As a small-firm user, I want future product pricing to use app-managed credits plus overage, so that I do not have to manage provider API keys in the product.
20. As a CLI pilot user, I want to use OPENAI_API_KEY, so that early experiments can run before product billing exists.
21. As a tenant admin, I want full-topology model context to require explicit opt-in, so that sensitive plant topology is not sent to a provider by default.
22. As a tenant admin, I want a maximum LLM context policy, so that I can control whether the model receives only the predicate contract, scoped context, or full topology.
23. As a security reviewer, I want no full prompt transcript retained by default, so that prompt logs do not become a sensitive data archive.
24. As a security reviewer, I want a minimal logic-request audit record, so that routing, model, context policy, confirmation, artifacts, and diagnostics are traceable.
25. As a maintainer, I want the LLM provider behind an adapter, so that OpenAI can be replaced later by Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Anthropic, or enterprise endpoints.
26. As a maintainer, I want v1 to avoid autonomous agent tool-calling, so that repository-owned code controls execution and artifacts.
27. As a maintainer, I want live OpenAI calls excluded from CI, so that tests are deterministic and do not require secrets.
28. As a maintainer, I want fake-provider tests, so that routing, drafting, repair, confirmation, and execution behavior can be validated without network calls.
29. As a maintainer, I want generated Datalog constrained to a safe Souffle subset, so that user-facing LLM-authored logic cannot include arbitrary includes, inputs, files, or external functors.
30. As a maintainer, I want generated helper predicates to be namespaced, so that LLM-authored relations do not collide with approved predicates.
31. As a maintainer, I want generated recursive predicates allowed with runtime limits, so that topology questions remain expressible.
32. As a maintainer, I want max output rows, Datalog size, relation count, and execution timeout limits, so that generated logic cannot create unbounded output or runaway execution.
33. As a future product owner, I want saved logic requests and standard rule packs deferred, so that v1 focuses on confirmed execution before persistence and promotion.
34. As a future product owner, I want the design to leave room for HAZOP and EPA-related standard rule packs, so that validated bundled checks can come later.
35. As a future enterprise buyer, I want deployment-tiered LLM privacy, so that small users can use managed APIs while larger firms can later use approved Azure, Bedrock, BYOC, VPC, or on-prem options.
36. As a future integration user, I want BioWin and simulation integrations deferred, so that v1 does not overclaim hydraulic or thermodynamic reasoning.
37. As a future multimodal user, I want image/SVG reasoning deferred, so that the initial trust boundary remains DEXPI XML to pyDEXPI graph to facts to Datalog.
38. As a reviewer, I want generated logic artifacts to be compact, so that the system does not produce excessive side files for every request.
39. As a reviewer, I want missing-capability artifacts to feed roadmap learning, so that unsupported questions reveal the next predicates or extraction projections needed.
40. As a reviewer, I want deterministic result artifacts and generated Datalog preserved, so that an answer can be reproduced and inspected later.

## Implementation Decisions

- The canonical product object is a logic request, not separate query and rule authoring flows.
- Saving logic requests for reuse is out of the first implementation; the user may eventually decide to save a confirmed logic request later.
- V1 is CLI-artifact-first rather than API/server-first.
- V1 adds an optional refine step that improves a vague logic request into a clearer request with assumptions, clarifying questions, route hints, and recommended scope.
- V1 adds a draft step that routes a logic request and, for topology logic, asks OpenAI to generate Datalog plus a formal engineer-readable restatement.
- V1 adds an execute step that requires confirmation before running generated Datalog against real derived graph semantics.
- The execution input is an existing derived_graph_semantics.dl artifact, not raw DEXPI XML.
- Python orchestrates the workflow. The LLM does not directly call Souffle, shell, filesystem, DEXPI extraction, BioWin, web search, or other tools.
- OpenAI is the first provider. The first CLI slice reads credentials from OPENAI_API_KEY.
- The model is configurable, with a high-accuracy default and cost optimization deferred.
- The provider integration should sit behind a small internal adapter. Do not adopt an agent framework for v1.
- V1 is text-only. Multimodal diagram, SVG, screenshot, and vision inputs are deferred.
- The router supports topology logic, metadata lookup, documentation answer, missing capability, clarification, and future external-tool-required outcomes.
- Only generated-Datalog requests require paired restatement confirmation.
- The LLM receives the predicate contract and synthetic tutorial facts by default, not customer plant facts.
- Tenant-level context policy should support contract-only, scoped-context, and full-topology levels. Full-topology context requires tenant admin opt-in in product form.
- No full prompt transcript is retained by default. Persist a minimal logic-request audit record instead.
- The draft artifact should be compact: one logic_request.json plus generated_query.dl as the only draft sidecar when needed.
- The formal restatement is stored inside the draft artifact rather than as many separate files in v1.
- The deterministic execution result remains primary. Any LLM explanation is supplemental.
- Generated Datalog uses only the approved predicate contract by default.
- Approved default predicates include node/1, node_label/2, node_tag/2, node_proteus_id/2, composition_edge/3, reference_edge/3, candidate_topology_edge/3, downstream_candidate/2, downstream_composition/2, downstream_reference/2, reachable/2, and direct_process_connection/2 marked experimental.
- Generic node_attribute/3 and graph_edge_attribute-style raw attributes are excluded by default and allowed only in advanced raw-attribute mode.
- Generated Datalog may define new namespaced helper predicates, including recursive helpers, if they compile and stay within runtime limits.
- Generated Datalog must not use .input, .include, external functors, arbitrary file paths, undeclared outputs, or relation names that collide with approved predicates.
- Safety checks enforce approved predicates, namespaced generated relations, declared output relations, maximum Datalog size, maximum generated relation count, timeout, and row limits.
- Repair attempts are bounded to two retries after an invalid generated program.
- Unsupported logic requests produce missing-capability artifacts rather than best-effort answers.
- Saved logic, trusted rule promotion, standard HAZOP/EPA rule packs, app-managed credits, BYOC, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, VPC deployment, and on-prem model deployment are future product work.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should use the highest public seam: CLI commands and persisted artifacts.
- Tests should not assert private prompt construction details unless those details are part of a public artifact contract.
- Normal CI must not require a live OpenAI key or network access.
- Use a fake LLM provider for deterministic tests of routing, drafting, repair, restatement, confirmation, and execution behavior.
- Add a test seam for a mocked valid topology logic request that drafts Datalog and restatement into a compact logic request artifact.
- Add a test seam for an invalid generated Datalog response that enters a bounded repair loop and then succeeds or fails with diagnostics.
- Add a test seam for unknown predicate use that returns a missing-capability or safety diagnostic instead of executing.
- Add a test seam proving execute requires confirmation before running generated Datalog against derived semantics.
- Add a test seam proving confirmed generated Datalog runs against the checked-in derived graph semantics fixture and persists deterministic result artifacts.
- Add a test seam proving documentation and metadata requests route away from Datalog generation.
- Add a test seam proving raw attributes are rejected by default and allowed only in advanced raw-attribute mode.
- Add a test seam proving runtime guardrails such as output row limits, timeout configuration, and disallowed constructs are enforced at the command boundary.
- Existing prior art includes CLI and persisted-artifact tests for query-derived-graph, derive-graph-semantics, compile-rule, verify-suite, verify-raw-fixture, and review-only.
- Existing deterministic query artifacts provide a model for combined query Datalog, result JSON, diagnostics, and raw Souffle output directories.
- Live OpenAI quality should be evaluated through an optional manual eval command or fixture set, not required in CI.

## Out of Scope

- App/server UI.
- Product billing implementation.
- App-managed credit ledger.
- Customer API-key upload UI.
- Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, BYOC, VPC, or on-prem deployment implementation.
- Anthropic provider support in v1.
- Agent frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents SDK, Cline as runtime dependency, or autonomous tool-calling agents.
- Multimodal P&ID image/SVG/screenshot reasoning.
- Raw DEXPI XML execution input for logic requests.
- One-command raw DEXPI to LLM logic execution workflow.
- BioWin or other process simulation integrations.
- Hydraulic, thermodynamic, sizing, or EPA/HAZOP compliance packs.
- Standard rule-pack authoring and promotion lifecycle.
- Saving logic requests for reuse.
- Deterministic Datalog-to-English compiler.
- Full prompt transcript retention by default.
- Full-topology prompt context by default.
- LLM-generated patch proposals or autocorrection.

## Further Notes

The central product principle remains unchanged: deterministic execution answers compliance and engineering logic questions; the LLM may refine, route, draft, repair, restate, and explain, but it is not the answer source.

The first implementation should optimize for learning whether frontier models can reliably draft useful Datalog against the repo-owned predicate contract. The CLI-artifact workflow should preserve enough evidence to debug failures without turning prompt logs into sensitive archives.

The long-term product can evolve toward app-managed credits plus overage for small customers, enterprise model/provider controls for larger customers, standard rule packs for recognized review frameworks, and private deployment options. Those future tiers should reuse the same logic-request, predicate-contract, confirmation, and deterministic execution concepts proven by the CLI slice.

title: PRD: Template-first hybrid grounded QA in the existing harness
description:
## Problem Statement

Process engineers asking read-only engineering questions currently face two disconnected reasoning paths. The benchmark-proven Arm T path can bind a question to trusted prebuilt logic cheaply and reliably, but it is not available through the product's existing grounded-QA harness. The product's generated-Datalog path can express novel topology questions, but its older workflow pauses for confirmation and does not yet provide the replacement semantic-faithfulness safeguards required for automatic execution. Users should not need to understand which path applies, approve template fit, inspect raw Datalog before every read-only query, or wait through a rigid repair-count limit. They need the existing grounded-QA workflow to select the cheapest faithful path, execute validated deterministic logic automatically, expose useful progress without revealing private chain of thought, and fail transparently rather than guess.

## Solution

Extend the existing restricted grounded-QA harness into a template-first hybrid workflow. The model remains responsible for planning among domain-approved capabilities, while the backend remains authoritative for capability permissions, cheap-first ordering, route receipts, template and generated-query validation, deterministic execution, artifacts, evidence, and interruption. A question that faithfully matches a bundled query template runs automatically after backend validation. A template no-fit or unrecoverable template failure produces a request-bound route receipt that unlocks generated Datalog. Temporary generated Datalog runs automatically only after mechanical safety validation and layered semantic-faithfulness verification. Read-only execution never requires user confirmation. Users receive a structured execution trace and post-execution semantic disclosure, and may steer a run with Answer Now or Stop. If no validated verdict exists, the system reports established facts and blockers rather than an ungrounded estimate.

## User Stories

1. As a process engineer, I want a read-only engineering question to run automatically when a bundled query template faithfully represents it, so that I receive a grounded answer without an unnecessary confirmation step.
2. As a process engineer, I want the system to choose the cheapest faithful reasoning path, so that routine questions do not incur generated-query cost and latency.
3. As a process engineer, I want template selection to preserve every explicitly named equipment class, so that the result covers the complete question rather than a plausible subset.
4. As a process engineer, I want template selection to preserve graph scope, so that piping-only and instrumentation-inclusive questions are not conflated.
5. As a process engineer, I want template selection to preserve direction, so that directed and undirected connectivity questions produce the intended result.
6. As a process engineer, I want classes absent from the current drawing to remain in reusable query bindings, so that the semantic scope of my question is not silently narrowed by current data.
7. As a process engineer, I want a question with no faithful template match to fall back to generated Datalog automatically, so that novel questions remain answerable.
8. As a process engineer, I want approximate template matches rejected conservatively, so that lower cost never takes priority over semantic correctness.
9. As a process engineer, I want ambiguous question meaning to trigger clarification rather than a guessed route, so that the executed logic represents my intent.
10. As a process engineer, I want permission and defeasible-exception questions to abstain or request human review, so that monotone topology logic does not issue an unsound deontic verdict.
11. As a process engineer, I want generated Datalog checked for safety before execution, so that temporary logic cannot escape the approved fact base, predicate contract, output contract, or resource boundary.
12. As a process engineer, I want generated Datalog checked for semantic faithfulness before execution, so that a tidy result cannot answer the wrong question.
13. As a process engineer, I want every generated-query revision revalidated, so that repair cannot introduce a new semantic error.
14. As a process engineer, I want uncertain or conflicting faithfulness evidence to fail closed, so that automatic execution is never authorized by ambiguity.
15. As a process engineer, I want a model semantic verifier to be able to veto or request repair but not authorize execution alone, so that model self-agreement is not treated as proof.
16. As a process engineer, I want deterministic intent checks and applicable counterfactual probes to authorize generated execution, so that the trust decision is grounded in inspectable evidence.
17. As a process engineer, I want operational engine failures distinguished from template no-fit, so that changing query authorship does not hide a shared execution outage.
18. As a process engineer, I want a generated-query failure to return diagnostics to the running agent, so that the agent can repair a concrete defect.
19. As a process engineer, I want the agent to continue through useful repairs without an arbitrary default attempt count, so that difficult but solvable questions are not cut off prematurely.
20. As a process engineer, I want to optionally constrain turns, duration, provider cost, or available capabilities, so that I can control a run when my context requires it.
21. As a process engineer, I want to click Answer Now during a long run, so that I can receive the best completed grounded state without waiting for further exploration.
22. As a process engineer, I want Answer Now to state clearly when no validated verdict exists, so that immediacy does not turn an estimate into engineering evidence.
23. As a process engineer, I want to stop an active run, so that I retain control over latency and provider usage.
24. As a process engineer, I want a concise structured execution trace, so that I can understand which route, validations, and engine produced the answer.
25. As a process engineer, I want technical trace details to be expandable, so that the normal answer stays readable while the underlying Datalog, diagnostics, and evidence remain inspectable.
26. As a process engineer, I want generated Datalog shown after execution with an engineer-readable semantic restatement, so that I can audit what was run without approving it in advance.
27. As a process engineer, I want deterministic witness evidence attached to the answer, so that claims can be traced to the prepared source facts.
28. As a process engineer, I want repeated provider activity summarized rather than dumped, so that the trace remains useful during long runs.
29. As a process engineer, I want an exact retry or resumed run to reuse valid routing work, so that interruption does not force unnecessary provider calls.
30. As a process engineer, I want changed classes, scope, direction, source data, template catalog, or policy to invalidate an old route receipt, so that stale no-fit decisions cannot bypass a newly applicable template.
31. As an auditor, I want an auditable record of attempted paths, final route, template version and bindings or generated-program identity, validations, provider attribution, deterministic result, and abstention reason, so that the answer can be reconstructed without preserving a full prompt transcript.
32. As an auditor, I want every visible engineering claim backed by deterministic evidence or a validation artifact, so that trace prose is not mistaken for proof.
33. As an auditor, I want private model reasoning excluded from the trace, so that chain of thought is not represented as engineering evidence.
34. As a security reviewer, I want trace redaction and size policy applied independently of event kind, so that extensions cannot leak secrets or unbounded tool output.
35. As a security reviewer, I want automatic execution restricted to approved read-only capabilities, so that query convenience does not grant mutation or external side effects.
36. As a security reviewer, I want the model unable to forge route receipts, alter execution mode, bypass validators, or expand its own capability permissions, so that runtime policy remains backend-owned.
37. As a rule maintainer, I want bundled query templates to carry a versioned human-readable description, supported parameter contract, and bundled rule-pack trust, so that trusted logic is reviewable and reusable.
38. As a rule maintainer, I want invalid template bindings rejected without changing the trusted template body, so that runtime correction does not create new logic.
39. As a rule maintainer, I want generated logic to remain temporary after automatic execution, so that running a query never silently promotes it into a reusable rule.
40. As a rule author, I want reusable-rule promotion to remain a separate explicit authoring action, so that ad-hoc execution and persistent trust are not conflated.
41. As an application developer, I want the hybrid behavior implemented through the existing grounded-QA public seam, so that routing, lifecycle, source scope, evidence, and provider behavior are not duplicated.
42. As an application developer, I want the ordinary model/tool loop to follow established harness semantics, so that tool calls continue the run and a final response ends it without a bespoke semantic-progress engine.
43. As an application developer, I want a stable trace event envelope with extensible namespaced kinds, so that new capabilities can participate without changing a closed trace-step enum.
44. As an application developer, I want unknown trace kinds to receive a safe generic rendering, so that backend and extension evolution does not break the client.
45. As an application developer, I want capability authorization independent of trace rendering, so that emitting an event never grants permission.
46. As an application developer, I want route receipts scoped to normalized intent, source snapshot, template-catalog version, and policy version, so that fallback authorization is precise and replay-safe.
47. As an application developer, I want generated-Datalog capability gating enforced by a backend receipt precondition, so that prompt instructions are not the only cheap-first safeguard.
48. As an application developer, I want fake-provider integration tests at the public harness seam, so that CI proves behavior without paid model calls.
49. As an application developer, I want real local deterministic execution in integration tests, so that tests do not silently preserve a Python or regex stand-in.
50. As an operator, I want provider and infrastructure ceilings to remain enforceable, so that a model-driven run cannot become an unlimited server process.
51. As an operator, I want operational ceilings distinguished from user-selected answer constraints, so that service safety is not confused with reasoning quality.
52. As an operator, I want provider cost, latency, fallback reason, and final route recorded, so that cost per grounded answer can be measured.
53. As a product owner, I want template coverage reported separately from policy abstentions, so that coverage metrics are not inflated or penalized by intentionally unsupported questions.
54. As a product owner, I want conditional template correctness and false-route rate measured, so that template adoption is evaluated on faithfulness rather than raw usage.
55. As a product owner, I want generated-authoring avoided, fallback correctness, and cost per grounded answer measured, so that the hybrid's economic benefit can be evaluated.
56. As a product owner, I want the released workflow to contain no confirmation prompt for read-only template or generated-query execution, so that the intended low-friction experience is preserved.
57. As a product owner, I want the old confirmation workflow retained only as an internal migration safeguard, so that intermediate development never exposes unvalidated automatic execution.
58. As a product owner, I want a fresh SME-certified unseen holdout before a generalization claim, so that success on the frozen nine-question development matrix is not mistaken for production proof.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing restricted grounded-QA harness and its existing turn runner rather than creating a second router or adopting a general-purpose agent-framework runtime.
- Preserve the provider-neutral, repository-owned model/tool loop: authorized tool calls continue the run; a final response without tool calls ends it; user steering, policy blocks, provider failures, or operational unavailability may also end or interrupt it.
- Keep the model responsible for planning among domain capabilities, while the backend owns capability authorization, route receipts, validation, deterministic execution, source/evidence boundaries, artifacts, and interruption.
- Run the deontic policy gate before template or generated topology logic. Permission and defeasible-exception requests abstain or require human review; they never receive a monotone topology verdict.
- Introduce bundled query templates as source-independent, parameterized, versioned logic under bundled rule-pack trust. Each template has an engineer-readable description, supported query shape, parameter schema, semantic obligations, and version identity.
- Do not import production behavior from benchmark-owned modules. Promote the required template semantics into the trusted product logic layer while retaining benchmark fixtures as evaluation evidence.
- Use conservative template routing. The model may propose a template and bindings or indicate no fit; the backend accepts only an exact faithful match. There is no numerical confidence threshold and approximate fit is rejected.
- Validate template category, parameter types, ontology labels, explicit closed-list completeness, source and target roles, graph scope, direction, quantifier, negation, output shape, and applicable faithfulness obligations before execution.
- Permit correction after template binding rejection through the normal model-driven loop without a fixed default semantic-attempt count. A binding correction changes parameters, never the trusted template body.
- Execute a valid bundled query template automatically. The user's read-only engineering question supplies execution intent; neither the user nor the model performs a confirmation step.
- Produce typed route outcomes for template success, template no-fit, binding rejection, template faithfulness failure, template execution failure, deontic abstention, clarification, and reasoning-engine unavailability.
- Issue route receipts only from backend-owned routing and validation outcomes. Models may consume receipts but cannot create, assert, widen, or alter them.
- Bind a route receipt to normalized semantic intent, source/fact snapshot identity, template-catalog version, and policy version. Exact semantic retries may reuse it; relevant changes invalidate it.
- Require a valid no-fit or template-failure route receipt before the generated-Datalog capability is available. This enforces cheap-first ordering without a duplicate deterministic intent classifier.
- Distinguish semantic routing failure from shared operational failure. A reasoning-engine outage never unlocks generated logic merely to retry the same unavailable engine.
- Keep generated Datalog temporary and read-only. Automatic execution never grants reusable-rule trust or promotes logic into an authored rule pack.
- Replace per-query generated-Datalog confirmation with automatic generated-query execution after all mandatory gates pass.
- Retain mechanical Datalog safety validation over fact-base boundaries, approved predicates, output contract, disallowed constructs, resource restrictions, and deterministic execution inputs.
- Add a blocking semantic-faithfulness gate before generated execution and after every revision. Failure, uncertainty, or conflicting evidence prevents execution.
- Implement layered faithfulness verification. Deterministic structured-intent checks, Datalog contract inspection, and applicable counterfactual probes authorize execution. A model-produced back-translation may veto or request repair but cannot authorize execution by itself.
- Feed validation and execution diagnostics back into the existing model/tool loop for repair. Do not impose a fixed semantic repair count by default.
- Permit users to configure optional turn, duration, provider-cost, or capability constraints. These constraints may narrow a run but cannot disable validators, widen permissions, or replace operational ceilings.
- Keep provider, account, infrastructure, cancellation, and service-availability ceilings as deployment-owned operational safeguards rather than answer-quality strategy.
- Add Answer Now and Stop steering. Answer Now interrupts further exploration and synthesizes from completed validated artifacts; when no validated verdict exists, it returns established facts, rejected attempts, and the blocker without guessing.
- If an atomic read-only tool operation is already in flight when Answer Now is selected, cancel it when safe cancellation exists; otherwise allow the atomic operation to finish but launch no new exploratory operation.
- Use a structured execution trace as the user-visible projection of routing, validation, execution, tool, and evidence events. Do not expose raw chain of thought or system prompts.
- Use a stable trace event envelope containing event identity, parentage, extensible namespaced kind, status, concise summary, timestamps, and optional detail/evidence references.
- Keep event kinds open. Rendering policy controls visibility, redaction, grouping, size, and evidence requirements; unknown kinds receive a safe generic rendering.
- Present concise step rows by default and artifact-backed details on expansion. Repeated provider/tool activity may be grouped. Generated Datalog is collapsed but inspectable.
- After automatic generated-query execution, disclose the engineer-readable semantics, source scope, route, validation outcomes, inspectable Datalog, deterministic result, and evidence. Disclosure is not approval.
- Classify capability effects independently of trace kinds. Approved read-only retrieval and validated logic may run automatically; mutation, persistent promotion, customer-data transmission, material external cost, and other side effects require separate authorization or remain denied.
- Preserve one minimal logic-request audit record containing attempted routes, final route, route-receipt identity, template version and bindings or generated-program hash, validation outcomes, repair summary, provider attribution, deterministic result identity, evidence references, abstention reason, and cost/latency accounting. Do not persist a full prompt transcript by default.
- Keep the old generated-query confirmation path only behind an internal unreleased migration guard until automatic execution, layered faithfulness, disclosure, steering, and end-to-end tests are complete. The released hybrid workflow has no read-only query confirmation prompt, and the legacy path is removed after cutover.
- Deliver in small vertical slices. The first slice runs one representative bundled-template topology question end to end through the existing public turn runner, automatically returning deterministic answer, witnesses, route artifact, and trace without generated Datalog or confirmation. Later slices add no-fit gating, generated execution and faithfulness, web trace/disclosure, steering, unseen holdout, and legacy removal.
- Update stale router and execution PRD language that treats all generated read-only logic as confirmation-gated or excludes restricted model-driven capability planning. Continue to reject unrestricted autonomous agents and a new general-purpose agent-framework dependency.

## Testing Decisions

- Test observable behavior through the existing public grounded-QA turn runner as the primary seam. Do not add a parallel router seam and do not assert on private prompt construction or internal helper calls.
- Use the existing web turn-lifecycle and review-flow boundaries only for streamed trace, Answer Now, Stop, and migration-state integration tests that cannot be observed through the primary runner alone.
- Start with one red behavior test: a representative equipment-to-pump connectivity question covered by a bundled query template executes automatically through the public runner, returns the correct deterministic verdict and witnesses, records the template route and bindings, emits trace events, never calls generated Datalog, and never enters a confirmation state.
- Use scripted fake model providers for deterministic routing and repair behavior in normal CI, following existing grounded-QA harness prior art.
- Execute trusted templates and generated programs against real local Souffle and checked-in prepared-fact fixtures in integration tests. Do not mock the deterministic engine when proving execution behavior.
- Reuse existing bundled-rule, temporary-Datalog, grounded-QA harness, turn-lifecycle, evidence, and benchmark fixtures as prior art. Extend public-contract assertions rather than replacing them with tests of subprocess details.
- Add behavior tests for complete and incomplete explicit class bindings, classes absent from the current drawing, directed and undirected queries, piping-only and instrumentation-inclusive scope, positive and negated conditions, and source/target reversal.
- Add behavior tests proving conservative template no-fit for semantically similar but unsupported questions.
- Add behavior tests proving one question may repair a rejected binding through subsequent model tool calls without changing the trusted template body.
- Add behavior tests proving a backend route receipt is required before generated Datalog, cannot be forged by a model response, and cannot be reused after intent, source, catalog, or policy changes.
- Add behavior tests proving an exact resumed semantic request may reuse a valid receipt.
- Add behavior tests proving template no-fit and template faithfulness failure may unlock generated logic while reasoning-engine unavailability does not.
- Add behavior tests proving deontic permission and defeasible-exception requests abstain without executing template or generated logic.
- Add behavior tests proving generated Datalog never executes after mechanical safety failure, deterministic faithfulness failure, uncertain faithfulness, conflicting verifier evidence, or exhausted useful repair.
- Add behavior tests proving a model verifier cannot authorize execution when deterministic obligations or probes fail.
- Add behavior tests proving every generated revision passes the complete gate sequence before automatic execution.
- Add behavior tests proving successful generated execution produces deterministic results, evidence, post-execution disclosure, and no read-only confirmation state.
- Add behavior tests proving automatic execution does not promote generated logic or grant reusable-rule trust.
- Add behavior tests proving capability effect policy permits approved read-only operations but blocks or separately authorizes mutation, persistence, external side effects, and restricted data transmission.
- Add behavior tests proving Answer Now returns an existing validated result when available and otherwise returns established facts and a clear no-validated-verdict status without launching new tools.
- Add behavior tests proving Stop terminates the run cleanly and preserves the completed audit trail.
- Add behavior tests proving optional user constraints narrow a run while validation, capability policy, and operational ceilings remain non-overridable.
- Add trace contract tests for event parentage, namespaced kinds, safe unknown-kind rendering, artifact references, redaction, bounded summaries, grouping, and deterministic evidence links.
- Add migration tests proving automatic mode cannot activate with missing mandatory validators and proving the legacy confirmation path is absent from the released configuration after cutover.
- Preserve existing direction-review confirmation behavior for inferred structural direction; removing read-only Datalog confirmation must not silently remove unrelated human review requirements.
- Run relevant existing QA, verification, web lifecycle, and benchmark regression suites after each slice, then the full repository suite before closing implementation beads.
- Perform an optional live-model verification after scripted integration tests prove wiring. The live run must preserve provider accounting and route artifacts but is not required in normal CI.
- Require a fresh SME-certified unseen holdout before a production generalization claim. Include template-fit, deliberate no-fit, ambiguous, explicit and implicit class scope, directed and undirected, piping and instrumentation, deontic abstention, and generated-repair cases. Treat correct conservative fallback as success.

## Out of Scope

- A second router or deterministic application-owned intent classifier parallel to the existing grounded-QA harness.
- Adoption of LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Vercel AI SDK, or another general-purpose agent runtime as a v1 dependency.
- An unrestricted autonomous coding agent, arbitrary shell access, unrestricted filesystem access, unrestricted network access, or model-owned execution.
- Raw private chain-of-thought display or persistence.
- A bespoke semantic-progress fingerprint engine in v1; repetition telemetry may justify a later stop condition.
- A fixed default semantic repair-attempt count; users may choose constraints and deployments retain operational ceilings.
- Automatic source-graph mutation, P&ID correction, design approval, issue creation, external-system writes, or other side effects.
- Redesign of authored-rule promotion or removal of author confirmation for persistent reusable rules.
- A complete deontic permission or defeasible-exception reasoning engine; v1 continues to abstain or require human review.
- Cross-session, cross-source, or multi-file reasoning beyond the existing single-file review-session contract.
- Hydraulic, thermodynamic, simulation, sizing, or external-standards calculations not represented by approved facts and predicates.
- Product billing, credit-ledger, provider-account, BYOC, VPC, or on-prem deployment implementation.
- A deterministic general-purpose natural-language-to-Datalog compiler.
- A full prompt transcript archive.
- Claiming production generalization from the frozen nine-question RMSO matrix.

## Further Notes

Arm T achieved 9/9 grounded credit on the frozen v3 development matrix at approximately $0.03150, while Arm C achieved 8/9 at approximately $0.09163. Arm T used seven bundled-template-style routes and two policy abstentions with zero fallbacks and materially lower cost per grounded credit. These results justify the template-first fast path but are regression/development evidence, not an unseen product holdout.

The canonical vocabulary and architectural decisions are recorded in the root domain glossary and ADRs covering the web-native grounded agent harness, one Souffle engine, automatic validated generated-Datalog execution, extensible governed execution traces, route receipts, and model-driven runs with optional user constraints.

The agreed primary test seam is the existing public grounded-QA turn runner. The first implementation slice should be behavior-driven and prove one real bundled query template end to end before adding the generated fallback path.

title: Hybridize trusted-template validation and require gate repair before giving up
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9

## What to build

Replace the literal request-text keyword/phrase matching in the bundled `equipment_without_pump_path` template validator with real semantic validation grounded in the graph and the model's declared structured intent, so the model can actually exercise judgment (not just echo magic words) when proposing a template. Allow subset class bindings validated against what is present/reachable in the loaded source instead of demanding an exact match to the full static catalog every time. Separately, stop letting a turn terminate in `faithfulness.no_faithful_program` after a single rejected generated-Datalog attempt when the rejection carried concrete repair guidance and round budget remains -- require at least one repair attempt first.

## Findings this is based on

- Prototype terminal session (pydexpi_datalog/web/prototype_qa_turn_repl.py) against the real turn flow with a live OpenRouter model.
- `_validate_equipment_without_pump_path` in pydexpi_datalog/qa/trusted_templates.py rejects any request whose raw text does not literally contain every class name plus magic phrases ("piping path", "in either direction", "every", " no piping path") -- this is keyword matching, not semantic validation, and none of these required phrases are disclosed to the model via pydexpi_datalog/qa/capability_manifest.py's tool description.
- `_require_class_binding` requires an *exact set* match against the full closed class catalog, so the model cannot bind just the classes actually present in a given drawing.
- The source_classes/target_classes binding roles are validated backwards from their intuitive meaning (source_classes checked against the pump classes, target_classes against the equipment classes).
- Observed live: a well-formed generated-Datalog proposal was rejected for a declared-intent/actual-query mismatch, the rejection message told the model to revise and call propose_temporary_datalog again, 14 of 20 rounds remained, and the model simply answered instead of retrying -- producing an unsatisfactory no-verdict answer for a question that was very likely answerable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Template binding validation no longer requires literal substring presence of class names or fixed magic phrases in the raw request text.
- [ ] Template binding validation accepts a true subset of the catalog classes, validated against the classes actually present/reachable in the loaded source rather than a fixed closed-set equality check.
- [ ] source_classes/target_classes binding roles are named and validated consistently with their documented meaning (equipment vs. pump), fixing the inverted check.
- [ ] The capability manifest's tool description for the bundled template no longer implies request-text keyword requirements that do not reflect the actual (now semantic) validation contract.
- [ ] The harness requires at least one repair attempt (a subsequent propose_temporary_datalog call incorporating the prior rejection's diagnostics) before returning faithfulness.no_faithful_program, whenever round budget remains.
- [ ] Existing template, structured-intent, counterfactual, faithfulness-gate, and harness regression suites pass, plus new tests covering subset bindings, semantic validation, and forced-repair behavior.
- [ ] Run relevant QA, verification, and full repository regression suites.
notes: Replaced literal request-text keyword/phrase matching in the equipment_without_pump_path validator with structural semantic validation: bindings renamed to self-documenting equipment_classes/pump_classes (fixing the inverted source/target naming), any non-empty duplicate-free subset of the supported catalog is accepted, and validation is graph-grounded via an absent_classes disclosure listing bound classes with no instance in the loaded source (absence is vacuously legitimate, never a rejection). Capability manifest now discloses the closed class catalog as per-item enums plus subset guidance instead of implying request-text keyword requirements. Harness now forces at least one repair attempt (MIN_FAITHFULNESS_GATE_ATTEMPTS_BEFORE_GIVING_UP=2) before a premature final answer can end the turn in faithfulness.no_faithful_program while round budget remains; exhausted budget still gives up cleanly. Deliberate deviation noted: graph-grounded validation discloses absent classes rather than rejecting them, since rejecting would break legitimate vacuous-truth questions (e.g. no tanks on the drawing => no violation). Validation: full suite 743 passed / 6 skipped / 123 subtests; scoped Ruff format+lint clean; Pyright at pre-existing baseline (no new errors); two-axis standards/spec review run with findings addressed (named retry constant, single diagnostics computation, graph-grounded disclosure).
close_reason: Hybridized trusted-template validation (subset bindings, semantic checks, graph-grounded absence disclosure, self-documenting binding roles, catalog disclosure in tool schema) and enforced one mandatory repair attempt before no_faithful_program; 743 tests pass.

title: Surface model reasoning and tool arguments in turn progress and trace
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9

## What to build

Request reasoning tokens from OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible providers when the selected model advertises reasoning support, capture that reasoning text (and each tool call's arguments) instead of discarding them, and thread them through the QA harness's per-round progress channel and the structured execution trace built in 3qo.9.6 -- so both the live in-flight state and the persisted trace show what the model considered and attempted, not just a bare tool name.

## Findings this is based on

- Prototype terminal session (pydexpi_datalog/web/prototype_qa_turn_repl.py), comparing the live per-round signal against harnesses like OMP, Codex, and Claude Code, which surface reasoning text and tool call arguments/results as they happen.
- pydexpi_datalog/qa/openai_compatible_qa_provider.py's chat/completions request never sets a reasoning parameter, so reasoning-capable models are never asked to return their reasoning trace.
- `_interpret()` in that same provider only reads `message["tool_calls"]` and `message["content"]"; any `reasoning`/`reasoning_content` field a model does return is silently discarded, and is not carried on `ToolCall`/`FinalAnswer`.
- `RoundProgress = Callable[[int, int, str | None], None]" in pydexpi_datalog/qa/grounded_qa_harness.py only carries round index, max rounds, and tool name -- not even the tool call's arguments -- so there is nowhere for reasoning or tool-input detail to go even if it were captured.
- pydexpi_datalog/web/turn_lifecycle.py's append_progress persists only that same thin shape to the turn's event log, which is what both the live /events stream and the final turn payload expose today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The OpenAI-compatible provider requests reasoning tokens for models/providers that advertise reasoning support, and does not regress providers/models that do not.
- [ ] Provider response parsing captures reasoning content and tool-call arguments instead of discarding them, and carries both on `ToolCall`/`FinalAnswer`.
- [ ] The round-progress channel (`RoundProgress` and `append_progress`) carries tool arguments and reasoning text, not just tool_name and round index.
- [ ] Reasoning and tool-argument content passing through the progress channel and the execution trace is bounded and redacted using the same allowlist/redaction discipline 3qo.9.6 established for trace details (no secrets, no unrestricted raw output).
- [ ] Live round-progress and the persisted structured execution trace both surface reasoning/tool-argument detail where available, and degrade gracefully (no crash, no leak, no fabricated content) when a model or provider does not supply it.
- [ ] Existing QA harness, provider, turn-lifecycle, and execution-trace regression suites pass, plus new tests covering reasoning capture, redaction, and graceful degradation.
- [ ] Run relevant QA, web lifecycle, and full repository regression suites.
notes: Implemented reasoning and tool-argument visibility across the provider -> harness -> web progress chain. OpenAI-compatible provider now sends the unified reasoning parameter for providers that advertise it (OpenRouter; gated per provider because other OpenAI-compatible endpoints reject unknown request fields -- OpenRouter itself normalizes the parameter per model, so model-level gating is delegated to the gateway) and captures reasoning/reasoning_content from responses onto ToolCall/FinalAnswer, never fabricating absent reasoning. RoundProgress widened to (round, max_rounds, tool_name, tool_input, reasoning); harness records bounded reasoning (MAX_TRACE_REASONING_LENGTH=2000, single source of truth imported by the web layer) into tool_call_trace, which flows into proposal/audit records. append_progress persists sanitized tool arguments (allowlist-style key blocking for credential/prompt-like keys, bounded strings/lists/depth) and bounded reasoning into the turn event log served by the live /events stream and the persisted turn record. Interpretation note: per ADR 0002/0010, model reasoning is prose and is surfaced through the persisted progress/audit channel rather than promoted into deterministic execution-trace envelopes. Validation: 751 passed / 6 skipped / 123 subtests; new provider test file (6 tests), enriched harness progress tests, web redaction/bounding test; Ruff clean on changed files; Pyright zero errors on web files and provider baseline unchanged; review_api diff kept to the scoped hunk after review flagged formatting churn.
close_reason: Reasoning tokens requested and captured, tool arguments and bounded/redacted reasoning surfaced through live round progress and persisted turn records; 751 tests pass.

title: Treat deterministic template verdicts as source grounding
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9

## What to fix

A grounded-QA answer backed by a successful bundled-template execution is stamped with the unsupported-source-claim disclosure ('This answer is not backed by validated evidence from your loaded source...') whenever the deterministic verdict is no_violation. _resolve_grounding in pydexpi_datalog/qa/grounded_qa_harness.py decides posture consistency purely from response.evidence_references; a no_violation verdict has zero witnesses, so there is nothing to cite, and the model's correct source_grounded declaration is downgraded to POSTURE_UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE_CLAIM -- even though the answer is backed by the strongest evidence the system produces (validated bindings + real Souffle over the loaded graph, with a route artifact).

Observed live in the prototype REPL: template accepted and executed, verdict no_violation, answer correct, disclosure attached anyway. violation_found answers dodge the bug only because witnesses exist to cite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An answer finalized on the same turn as an answered execute_bundled_query_template result counts that deterministic result as source grounding, with or without witnesses.
- [ ] no_violation template answers declared source_grounded keep POSTURE_SOURCE_GROUNDED, source_grounded=True, and carry no unsupported-source-claim disclosure.
- [ ] Fabricated or unrelated source claims without either citations or a deterministic result still downgrade to POSTURE_UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE_CLAIM exactly as today.
- [ ] Regression coverage through the public run_grounded_qa_turn boundary for both verdict polarities.
- [ ] Run QA and full repository regression suites.

title: Progress sanitizer drops scalars in nested tool arguments
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9

## What to fix

_sanitize_progress_value in pydexpi_datalog/web/execution_trace.py returns None for ANY value at depth >= 3, including leaf scalars. tool_input -> bindings (dict) -> equipment_classes (list) -> class-name strings sit at depth 3, so the live progress channel displays 'equipment_classes': [] / 'pump_classes': [] even though the real tool call carried the full class lists. Observed live in the prototype REPL immediately after 3qo.9.12 landed: the reasoning text says 'include all of these' while the rendered tool_input shows empty lists -- actively misleading the reviewer the channel exists to inform.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The depth cap limits container nesting, not leaf scalars: strings/numbers/bools inside lists inside one nested mapping survive sanitization (bounded as usual).
- [ ] Redaction (blocked key parts) and string/list/key bounds behave exactly as today.
- [ ] Regression test covers a propose/execute-shaped tool_input with nested class lists surviving into the persisted progress event.
- [ ] Run web lifecycle and full repository regression suites.

title: Reject generated queries that violate structured intent
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9

## What to build

A generated query reaches the existing execution boundary only when its mechanically inspectable semantics preserve the user’s structured logic intent; mismatches return precise diagnostics to the normal model-driven repair loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mechanically compare requested and encoded classes, quantifier, negation, source/target roles, graph scope, direction, and output obligations.
- [ ] Reject a program that compiles but reverses roles, narrows explicit class scope, changes edge scope, changes direction, or changes polarity.
- [ ] Return structured mismatch diagnostics that the running model can use for repair.
- [ ] Allow subsequent materially revised programs through the normal model/tool loop without a fixed default semantic-attempt count.
- [ ] Keep the temporary generated-query confirmation migration behavior unchanged in this slice.
- [ ] Test valid, invalid, and repaired programs through the public grounded-QA turn runner.

title: Replay counterfactual faithfulness probes before execution
description:
## Parent

## What to build

- [ ] Select mandatory probes from the normalized intent and predicate contract rather than benchmark question identifiers.

title: Compose the blocking layered faithfulness gate
description:
## Parent

pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9

## What to build

The production semantic-faithfulness gate combines structured-intent checks, Datalog contract inspection, counterfactual probes, and an optional model-verifier veto into one fail-closed decision for generated logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Authorize progression only when deterministic semantic obligations and applicable counterfactual probes pass.
- [ ] Permit a model-produced back-translation to veto or request repair but never to authorize execution by itself.
- [ ] Treat conflicting, incomplete, or uncertain faithfulness evidence as failure.
- [ ] Run the complete gate after every generated revision.
- [ ] Return a missing-capability result with established diagnostics when no faithful program is produced.
- [ ] Never return an ungrounded engineering verdict from an exhausted run.
- [ ] Verify gate decisions and repair behavior through the public grounded-QA turn runner.

## Blocked by

- pydexpi-datalog-1-3qo.9.4 — Replay counterfactual faithfulness probes before execution
notes: Implemented fail-closed layered semantic-faithfulness gate across mechanical validation, structured-intent comparison, mandatory counterfactual probes, and optional model-verifier veto. Every generated revision records bounded probe/gate outcomes; repair feedback is returned to the model; exhausted failed runs produce faithfulness.no_faithful_program and cannot be bypassed by a final answer. Layered evidence persists through proposal and confirmation audit records. Validation: 734 tests passed, 6 skipped, 123 subtests; changed files pass Ruff format/lint and git diff --check; new gate/audit modules pass Pyright. Repository-wide Pyright still reports 8 pre-existing errors outside the new gate ranges. Two-axis code review: no findings.
close_reason: Implemented layered semantic-faithfulness gate with repair, exhaustion protection, audit persistence, and full regression coverage (734 tests pass).
